A question that remains unanswered when criminal cases involve scenes of serial killers is why? Why do serial killers feel the need to act on their urges? What part of the personality has so much control that causes the concluding actions of a desire to end in the form of a life being taken? There are three parts to the personality that impact who we are and who we become. First, the social self pertains to the recognition we receive from others (how they see us in their minds). Second, the material self, which by all means is the one part of ourselves that changes least, is responsible for the things we claim and disclaim that all impact who we become. Lastly, the ego, which is responsible for how we see ourselves and is also subject to change the most. A significant driving force impacted by all three of these personality contributions is either a hyperactive nature and nurture influence during early childhood development or the total absence of a nature and nurture influence altogether. Serial killers are motivated by a strong force from the version of “me" that could be dangerous when not controlled. While all parts of the "self" play a role in outward behavior and interaction with others, the version of the self that thrives on stability is the ego. When the ego becomes uncontrollable, so does the individual.

In William James' The Self and Its Selves, the concept of self is analyzed. James claims that "In its widest possible sense, however, a man's self is the sum total of all that he CAN call his, not only his body and his psychic powers, but his clothes and his house, his wife and children, his ancestors and friends, his reputation and words, his lands and horses, and yacht and bank-account. All of these things give him the same emotion" (James, 122). In other words, every aspect of our lives plays a role in who we are as people. The daily interactions we unknowingly participate in have an impact on who we are; the slightest bit of change in tone during a conversation can have an unnoticed effect on our subconscious. When the things around us thrive and flourish, so do we. When the things around us crash and burn, so do we, in a way. Who we are can be respectively divided into four categories/sections belonging to two separate groups. The most active part of our personality is responsible for all of our interactions.

The part of who we are that strictly relies on others to function and is the easily most affected version of ourselves impacted by others, the Social Self. According to William James, the social self is the part of us that seeks validation from others, "A man's Social Self is the recognition which he gets from his mates" (James, 123). Social interactions play a vital role in the development of our brains and our emotions. When we are exposed to others at a young age, our brains start to register the "role" or "front" is used to interact with another person as the Social Self, "in very early childhood, new procedural memories for interacting with others and for regulating effects can be formed more easily than they can ever be again" (Tyson, Journal of the American Psychoanalytic Association). The lack of healthy interaction at such a young age suggests that children have a reduced development of their sense of agency, their ability to establish moral standards, their ability to assume self-responsibility, and have no capacity for emotional regulation. Many serial killers are victims of rejection at some point in their life. Due to the lack of interaction in early childhood, the rejection is more of a devastation than a simple awkward interaction, "it may seem to be counterintuitive on the surface, but many serial killers are actually insecure individuals who are compelled to kill due to a morbid fear of rejection. In many cases, the fear of rejection seems to result from having been abandoned by their mother in early childhood' (Bonn, Understanding What Drives Serial Killers). James refers to the lack of interaction or being "unnoticed by all members thereof" as the most "fiendish punishment that could be devised." Receiving validation from others is essential in developing our ability to understand and return self-expression to others.

The material self can pertain to the body, "the innermost part of the material self in each of us…" (James, 123). The things we own, such as clothes, also fit into this category because we use clothes to identify and showcase who we are to the outside world. In other words, we express ourselves through the things we call our own. Family applies to this category; the people who raise us, whether it is immediate family or not, become a part of who we are due to their influence on us as children. The role of the family in one's life is critically impacted when it comes to nature vs. nurture. When children are raised on love and affection, their outlook tends to be more positive and joyful. The opposite is in order for when children are raised on hatred and fear; their perspective tends to be more hostile and aggressive. During the infant stage, the sight of aggression in young children is expected due to the lack of self-expression available in their minds. This lack of self-expression results in few ways to attain attention to the issue the infant needs attention for, "both healthy and pathological aggression involve the intent to harm (in reality or fantasy) and tend to become accompanied with by unpleasant effects such as anger fear or frustration." (Fonagy, Aggression and the Psychological Self) From a young age, the lack of love and the integration of aggression leads to the exposure of violence due to the lack of self-expression available in the infant mind, he or she who is exposed to the hatred at such a young age will only grow and develop their own aversion to the ones who appeared to him/her, "They may come to believe that by destroying the person he desires prior to entering into a relationship with them, he can eliminate the frightening possibility of being abandoned, humiliated or otherwise hurt by someone he loves, as he was in childhood" (Bonn, Understanding What Drives Serial Killers). Until self-expression can be controlled, violence will continue to be a result of aggression, and it will only become a more driving force in the lives of those affected.

As humans continue to develop, the piece responsible for how a person feels about themselves does too. The part of the mind accountable for a person's sense of self-esteem or self-importance, "the ego is the component of personality that is responsible for dealing with reality" (Cherry, Id, Ego, and Superego Are Part of a Structural Model of Personality). Beginning in the early stages of development, through praise, verbal/nonverbal affirmations, and positive influences, the ego is created for a healthy mental state and positive self-esteem. These experiences are essential during the early stages of development because it healthily encourages self-love and appreciation. On the other hand, when there is a lack of affirmations and praises, it can have an even more significant impact than receiving the assurances. When children are exposed to feelings such as anger at such a young age, their physical development is impaired, "In these formulations, aggression is an annihilating presence in the infant. It is an anti-life, anti-self-force; an impediment to the development of the ego, rather than the ego's protest at the presence of impediments in the environment." (Fonagy, Aggression and the Psychological Self). In cases where aggression is all a child knows, there is no comprehensible version of positive emotions in their minds. When all the child knows is anger and fear, these emotions gaining strength from being present at a young age can result in the "wrong idea" about life in general; this “wrong idea” from childhood results in a bitter and hateful individual. The child that was raised on hatred only grows in rage as they age.

The concept in question is why serial killers are the way are they are. The answer to this question may seem complex, but I believe it is simple. Instead of the argument being nature vs. nurture, the concept being challenged should be either too much or not enough nature and nurture will result in a corrupt person, "It is futile to try to separate developmental influences on children into nature and nurture," says George Holden, chair of the department of psychology at Southern Methodist University. The "nature" part of child development refers to the individual's genetic make-up regarding development and learning. In other words, our nature is how we are predestined to develop and grow up. An example of how nature is responsible is when someone becomes a suspect for murder- a serial killer, their relatives and friends say, "that's not in his nature," referring to the fact that it could not possibly be the person they knew because "they are not capable" of that form of evil. Another example can be seen in the bible, "the sin nature manifested itself early in the genealogy: the very first child born to Adam and Eve, Cain, became the very first murderer" (Genisis 4:8). The concept of "nurture" is the general influence external pressures having on an individual, these influences ranging from family and upbringings to education. However, it has been proven that our genetic predisposition only has a growing impact on how we act. If children grow up in an entirely different environment from their parents, they are more likely to have a more substantial nurture impact. Theodore Wachs, a psychologist at Purdue University who studies child development, quoted, "if only because the environmental context, broadly conceived, that kids grow up in may be quite different from the environmental context their parents grew up in." Too much nature and nurture in a person can lead to dangerous outcomes. Not enough nature and nurture can lead to far more hazardous results; therefore, children must grow and develop a personality on their own terms.

The lack of social interaction that is now in effect because of the pandemic we are in is responsible for the growing aggression throughout the world. With this “new way of life” that is now being traditionalized in many homes, “seriously, given the severity of the coronavirus and how it is impacting us in the form of fear and inconvenience, those things that bothered us before the outbreak that began in Wuhan, China, in December—not even three months ago—don’t seem so bad after all. Coronavirus has put a lot into perspective” (Hyken, The Good Old Days). COVID-19 has removed a large number of components responsible for healthy development. Children born in this pandemic and children in their most prime developmental stage have all been deprived of at least one crucial part of the “me.” Without a solid contribution from each of the categories, social, material, and ego, children are likely to grow up with a heightened sense of aggression and a deficit of understanding right and wrong.

Serial killers and ordinary people all share the same components and concepts of the "Me." Each person, no matter their morals, has a social, material, and egotistical self. The differing factor comes into play during the early stages of life. In life, if the "normal" individual, love and affection are shown and implemented throughout the span of most their entire life. Beginning in early childhood up to when those responsible for the love and respect no longer exist, these individuals are shown positive reinforcement. Those who are raised on aggression and hatred follow a very different path of life. When all this individual is able to process is hatred and aggression, their ability to express compassion and love has now been rerouted to resulting in violence to express their desires. While the component of self is consistent from person to person, the development of these components in each individual varies extensively. Each variation of these features comes with its own identity; as James William would say, "the personal identity would not exist as a fact: but it would exist as a feeling all the same." Personal identity is not just the identity of the person; it is the environment around the person; it is their family or lack thereof, it is their interactions at a young age, it is the emotions they were exposed to as children. The material is self is what we are made of. The social self is who others say we are, and the ego self is who we say we are. When these three components are aligned, the future seems bright, but there is no way to predict the damage when these three components are not aligned.

chunks.label: Analysis of self, development, and serial killers
chunks.what_happened: The student analyzes William James's theories of the self (social self, material self, and ego) and the interplay of nature and nurture to examine the psychology and developmental roots of serial killers, concluding with reflections on the pandemic and a bibliography.

nd6b51944.title: Racial Discrimination in Hometown Restaurant Hiring

chunks.text: Is there equality between races within businesses? Automatically, it is thought that there is equality between races because all races now live together in society, but in reality, true equality has not been accomplished. Within society people create stereotypes of black people, assuming they are bad based on the color of their skin. Instead of getting to know a person and judging them based on their personality, people often get judged by how they look. This is because in the past black people were considered to be less than white people because of their skin color and this idea has continued to be passed down even though there is “equality” in today's world. Black people tend to have to work a lot harder than white people to get a job and even when they do it is common for them to be put in a position where they will not be seen by the public and it is not necessarily a good job.
chunks.label: Racial discrimination and stereotypes in the workplace
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on racial inequality and stereotypes in society, explaining how Black people face discrimination and job segregation due to historical biases.

chunks.text: Within my small, predominantly white, hometown I have worked at two different restaurants that are both very popular. The first restaurant is on the water, which people would often go to after a boat day. At this job, I worked as a hostess and a food runner. It was a very common place for high schoolers to work and needed many different people as servers, barbacks, and more. After I had applied, I told my friend, who is black, to apply as well because he has a good work ethic and social skills. When I told my boss about him, she said that they needed more servers, and he would most definitely get the job. However, when he came for his in-person interview, my boss told him that they did not have any space for him, and he could not have the job. I had asked my boss why he did not receive the job and she responded saying “he was not the right person to be a server” which did not make a lot of sense considering he had the skills for it. Later on in the year I had noticed that she went on to give many people jobs as servers and hosts, but all of them were white. However, back in the kitchen where customers were not able to go, all of the chefs and dishwashers were black.
chunks.label: Black friend rejected for server job at restaurant
chunks.what_happened: The student worked at a waterfront restaurant and encouraged a Black friend to apply for a server job. Despite being told they needed servers, the boss rejected him after an in-person interview, subsequently hiring only white servers while keeping Black workers in the kitchen.

chunks.text: The second place where I started to work was a country club. I started to notice the same trend of events, but worse. Within my first week there, I realized that all the kitchen staff and people that worked in the back were black. I was told by someone that had worked there longer than me that black people had applied to be servers but were told they were not the right fit for the job. One of the guys that worked in the kitchen came and welcomed me and told me if I had questions, he would be happy to help me out. A few of my coworkers had noticed and came up to me and told me to stay away from him and that he was bad. For them to say something like this led me to ask them why they had thought he was ‘bad’, and their answer was “he came from the hood which makes him bad”. The ‘hood’ in my town is the black community that everyone says to stay away from when in reality nothing bad has ever happened there. Even though he had never given my coworkers a reason to think he was bad, they were very quick to assume something about him because of where he came from.
chunks.label: Working at a country club with segregated roles
chunks.what_happened: The student worked at a country club where Black workers were relegated to the back and kitchen staff. When a Black kitchen worker kindly offered to help the student, coworkers warned the student to stay away because the worker came from the 'hood.'

chunks.text: After experiencing situations like this firsthand, I started to pay attention when eating at different restaurants. Within my hometown, there is not one restaurant that has a black server besides for the McDonalds. Most black people that work in a restaurant, are given a job of making food for someone else or cleaning up other people's messes. From some people’s point of view, these are jobs that are considered to be more appropriate for specific races. They are given jobs with less pay and where they are not noticed by customers.
chunks.label: Observing racial segregation in hometown restaurants
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on observing that restaurants across their hometown almost never hire Black servers, instead keeping them in low-paying kitchen or cleaning jobs out of public view.

chunks.text: Within the Pager Discrimination Study, Devah Pager did research on whether discrimination plays a role within a low-wage labor market. To find the answer, Pager used an experimental research method by sending out different races with equal resumes to find a job. Through the experiment, it was found that there are different discrimination mechanisms used by employers. The first mechanism is categorical exclusions which is when someone is not hired because of their race. The next is shifting standards which require a more intense interview based on someone’s race. Lastly, job channeling is when someone gets hired but is given a job that is considered to be more appropriate for their race. It is less likely for a minority to get a job because they are seen as unreliable, dishonest, or lacking social abilities causing them to have to try a lot harder than white people.
chunks.label: The Pager Discrimination Study and hiring mechanisms
chunks.what_happened: The student describes Devah Pager's research on racial discrimination in low-wage labor markets, defining categorical exclusion, shifting standards, and job channeling.

chunks.text: For a very long time, it has been a common occurrence for black people to be judged based on how they look. These judgments are often poor and tend to degrade black people. They are seen as bad people because of their skin tone. It is not common for a black person to be judged based on who they are. It is more common for them to be judged by how they look and where they come from.
chunks.label: Societal prejudice based on appearance
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on the ongoing tendency in society to degrade and judge Black people based on their appearance and background rather than character.

chunks.text: Both of the restaurants where I have worked have discriminated towards black people. Almost everyone on the staff was white and the bosses were older and still had certain beliefs that would not normally be accepted in today's society. The first and second restaurant partook in job channeling. Many people who had applied for a job there got the job that they had originally applied for, as long as they were white. On the other hand, when a black person had applied, they were automatically given a job that was more suitable for them. Those who worked in the kitchen where they were not visible to the public were placed in positions that the employer felt best fit them. Not only did they represent job channeling, but they also represented categorical exclusion. When a black person had applied for an open job, they were not given it because of how they looked. This is not an issue that only occurred within those restaurants, it is something that happens everywhere.
chunks.label: Analyzing workplace experiences using sociological concepts
chunks.what_happened: The student connects the two restaurant jobs to concepts of job channeling and categorical exclusion, noting that discrimination occurs widely.

chunks.text: Equality is something that everyone would like to believe in, but after many years there still does not seem to truly exist. Through my experiences within businesses, I have realized that there is still discrimination and both races are not treated equally because people are often quick to judge. Even though true equality has not yet been achieved, that does not mean it cannot. It is important for people to learn to get to know a person before creating ideas about them based on what they look like. Encourage employers to instead of using different discrimination mechanism, take the time to give black people an opportunity to prove that they can be trustworthy, reliable, and good workers. By doing so, it could create equality within businesses and inspire other people to not be so quick to judge.
chunks.label: Call for employers to end discriminatory practices
chunks.what_happened: The student concludes by reflecting on the lack of true racial equality and calls on employers to abandon discriminatory mechanisms and judge workers fairly.

nf3a393f9.title: Conforming to Gender Expectations in School

chunks.text: Throughout time over the past few decades society has evolved and constantly changed the definition of what it means to “do gender”, it has become new meanings on what a person needs to do to play the role of your assigned gender just to fit into societies standards, and to be viewed as normal. This has become new standards for women such as how they dress, how they have to act, especially when it comes to a man, and as well as their career path. For men, it has become an image of mainly how they have to act, and especially how they treat women. This normalization of what you should be doing to “do gender” ultimately has a negative impact on everyone’s lives.
chunks.label: Societal standards of doing gender
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on how society has evolved the definition of doing gender and argues that these rigid gender expectations harm everyone.

chunks.text:
I attended a private school for most of my life, so while I was there I witnessed a lot of examples of “doing gender”. It raised me to believe that these expectations that society has to fit into its standards of how each gender is supposed to play their role were normal. It taught me that if I were to show any emotion it would be seen by people as me being weak and that I would lose my sense as a man. Everyone that I was around all the time in school fit into these roles as well. All of the girls would wear the typical clothing society portrays, such as the short shorts, skirts, tank tops, leggings, and if a girl tried to wear any clothing that would classify them as a “tomboy”, they would instantly be judged by everyone else in the community.

On the other hand all of the guys in my school including myself because of how we were raised, and the community we were in based on the school, kind of fit into the typical toxic masculinity role. Ever since the start, we were extremely competitive in everything we did, and even things that were nowhere near a competition, we turned it into one. No matter what was going on in our lives, you would never see any of us show any sort of emotion or sadness, because we did not want to get made fun of, or looked at as weak by all of the other guys.

On top of making things a competition, the atmosphere was extremely hostile towards one another at all times. Although most of us were friends, there was a constant argument and people making fun of other people just to bring them down, to make themselves seem more powerful and superior. It usually tended to work too, because the louder the guy was the fewer guys would talk back to him.
chunks.label: Gender roles at private school
chunks.what_happened: The student describes attending a private school where students conformed to strict gender roles, including girls being judged for dressing like tomboys and boys adopting toxic masculinity by competing, hiding emotions, and putting each other down.
chunks.people: the student, peers, classmates, girls, boys, friends

chunks.text:
The question to this whole gender role stigma that both genders tend to face, is why this ideology is still practiced and upheld in society. Over time we have broken some of the typical traditions that both genders uphold especially when it comes to females. This goes back to the main three different waves of feminism which have completely changed the outlook on how women are supposed to act in society.

First wave feminism goes back to starting all the way in the 1870s when women were pushing to change the way America’s voting system worked where women were able to vote. This was important to breaking the chains of sexism and blindly following the idea of “doing gender”. Women began to realize that they can fight to become more of an equal presence in society, and hold more power. Instead of being seen as others, women fought to show that they are human too and it is not just the man who has power, and has an important role in society.

After the first wave of feminism, the second wave of feminism began shortly after World War II. Women became tired of not being seen as equals in the workforce, where men could only do the heavy work, and women tended to be stuck being a housewife and care for the husband and family, or do jobs that were seen as “less important in society”. They were able to fight once again and show that they are just as capable of playing an important role in the world, and it is not just men that have the control.

Finally, we have the third wave feminism which is still currently an issue, or also known as the sexual revolution. This allowed for a lot more inclusivity for women and to be able to live their lives and express themselves more freely. The consequence of this that I believe can be seen today, is the over-sexualization of women from men as well as in the marketing strategies. Women are now constantly having to deal with issues of catcalling and being seen as objects as well as subjects to sexual harassment. The marketing strategies do not help with this ideology and problem that society faces because they try to use women and the idea of sex appeal to help sell their idea and project.

This is all part of the idea of “doing gender”, because both genders fall into this role. Women are raised to believe that they are seen as objects and subjects to men, as bad as it sounds. And men are raised to believe that women are just simply objects and trophies to be shown off and obtained for self-gain and power by men. Now of course not all of society is raised to believe and think this way, but it tends to be the normal idea in smaller more private parts of the world, especially small towns in the south. This is because they keep the idea of how doing gender was seen a long time ago, and that idea just repeats itself over and over throughout generations.

This is also shown by the writing done by de Beauvoir, of how women are seen as lesser to men and viewed instead as an “other”. She goes on to discuss how men will never bring up their gender or start off something by describing how “I am a man”. She goes on to discuss how no one ever questions the ideology or beliefs a man has, simply because he is a man. But for women, she says from personal experience that women will get judged on their beliefs and told they are incorrect as she says, “You only think that because you’re a woman.” This goes to show the daily life and struggle especially as a woman to play this idea of gender roles and to do gender, especially when in society women have always been viewed and treated as inferior.

The examples of the three waves of feminism are important because it shows that society is capable of breaking ideas of doing gender, and how the two genders have to play their role in society. But it also shows that so far we have been incapable of being able to break this never-ending cycle of there always being some sort of standards in society that the genders have to uphold to be seen as normal.

What I believe can be learned from this analysis is that society needs to break this cycle that it has created of doing gender, and eliminate our idea as a whole of how we believe a certain gender should act or display themselves. Even the waves of feminism help back this up as well as statistics of mental health disorders and suicide rates of men. This chain will not be broken until both women and men can act how they would like and be viewed by society as equals, where both can have power and influence. As well as men developing the idea of it being okay to show weakness and show their emotion instead of society making them feel like they have to play the power-hungry role as well as the alpha dog role. Society would be better as a whole if we could break the cycle of “doing gender” and change the meaning behind it because ultimately it does more harm in the world than it does good.
chunks.label: Analysis of feminism and gender roles
chunks.what_happened: The student discusses the three waves of feminism, Simone de Beauvoir's writings on women as the 'other', and argues that society must break the harmful cycle of doing gender.

chunks.text: As long as homo sapiens has been walking, religion has been a huge part of motivation, interaction, and wellbeing. A lot of research has been done as to why people believe what they believe, and the validity of religious belief comes into question each time this is studied. Does religion have an impact on individuals? Does religion impact our interactions with others? While these can’t be answered definitively, there are strong cases from each side of the argument. This paper will primarily address the major effects of religion, both positive and negative, on individuals and societal interactions and the importance of religion or lack thereof in society.
chunks.label: Introduction to religion's impact on society
chunks.what_happened: The student introduces the topic of religion's influence on individual wellbeing and societal interactions, outlining the paper's scope.

chunks.text: The research studied in class by Maryanski and Turner about the neurology of religion intrigued me, and as a psychology and religion double major, I couldn’t help but become more and more fascinated by this concept the more I thought about it. As a religious person who is part of a religious community, I was told that it was a bad idea to research something that may argue against what I believe. But here I am doing it anyways, because how can I believe something without knowing the scientific processes of why I believe it, and why would I refuse to look at it from both sides? As I got further into this research, I saw that many sociologists and psychologists had contributed, as well as many renowned theologians. The contributions from both sides produced a well-rounded perspective that can help anybody realize that there are advantages and disadvantages to religion in a society that is rapidly turning away from it. Maryanski and Turner define the sociological perspective of religion as “More than just the propensity to behave in a religious manner. Religion is, at one and the same time, a neurological, behavioral, and organizational process (Maryanski and Turner, 2018).
chunks.label: Double major perspective on religion and neurology
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on their interest as a psychology and religion double major studying Maryanski and Turner's work despite warnings from their religious community.

chunks.text: The first question we must ask to see how religion impacts society is this: what are the effects of religious belief on individual wellbeing? Research from Christopher Ellison of Duke University suggests that religion enhances wellbeing in four ways. The first way that religion enhances wellbeing is through social integration and support. Humans have a longing for interaction with one another through various ways and being a part of a religious community helps satisfy this. The second way that religion enhances wellbeing is through the establishment of personal relationships with a divine other. This allows people to feel like they are specially made for a purpose, rather than a random result of evolutionary processes. The third way is through the provision of systems of meaning and existential processes, and like the second reason, this helps believers know that they have a purpose, and that humans exist for a reason greater than anyone can comprehend. The fourth way that religion enhances wellbeing is through the promotion of more specific patterns of religious organization and personal lifestyle (Ellison, 1991). Tying into Maryanski and Turner’s definition of religion, Ellison conducted a study on how religion affects individual wellbeing. He asked random individuals to rate from one (low) to eight (high) their satisfaction with community life, nonworking activities or hobbies, family life, friendships, and health or physical condition. Those five categories are what Ellison says comprise “overall wellbeing”. The study resulted in substantial evidence of a positive influence of strong religious faith on higher life satisfaction, greater personal happiness, and fewer negative psychosocial consequences of traumatic life events. The study also showed that religious individuals who were affiliated with a specific sect or denomination reported higher life satisfaction than their unaffiliated counterparts. This first study shows that religion has a positive effect on overall wellbeing of individuals, and that life satisfaction has a positive correlation to the strength of one’s faith.
chunks.label: Literature review on religion and wellbeing
chunks.what_happened: The student reviews Christopher Ellison's research regarding four ways religious involvement enhances subjective wellbeing and life satisfaction.

chunks.text:
The second question we must ask on how religion impacts society is this: how do religious communities interact with other communities, both religious and nonreligious? Similar to ethnocentrism, humans are drawn to those who share experiences, beliefs, and values, and religion helps unite them in that. However, while religion has a positive impact on the life satisfaction and general wellbeing of members of one group, groups often clash against one another because of various differences in belief or conflict of interests. One of the most notable examples of this is the Crusades. Early in the Second Millennium AD, Christians were encouraged to take up arms for what they believe and destroy all people who are nonbelievers. Another example is Islamic Jihad. While neither religion’s text calls for violence against others, misinterpretation of sacred text and fear of “the other” inspires members of religious communities to fight against other groups for political power or superiority. While members of religious groups interact well in smaller groups with members of other religions, the people in power and religious scholars tend not to associate with people who believe other things. The superiority complex of religious institutions is fascinating to me, that a group can believe that they have been ordained by their god to run the world. This makes religion sound like a perfect thing to create to generate income and gain support from people.

While some religions and sects don’t get along, many religions, namely Buddhism and other Asian religions, are encouraged to spread peace and love to everyone. Some sects of Christianity, like Presbyterians and Methodists, base the foundation of their theology not in conversion of others, but through the spread of their message through showing love to others, like the famous Christian hymn “They Will Know We Are Christians By Our Love”. The positive interactions between religious groups have led to the formation of so many awesome organizations and communities.
chunks.label: Intergroup religious dynamics and conflict
chunks.what_happened: The student discusses how religion can cause intergroup clash or cooperation, citing historical conflicts, religious texts, and peaceful denominations.

chunks.text: In my hometown of Raleigh, the Interfaith Food Shuttle is run by people of all religious backgrounds and served to everyone who needs it. My father, who is a Presbyterian minister, is good friends with an Imam, a Rabbi, and a Bhikkhuni. Every American holiday, they organize a service for upwards of five hundred people to celebrate and give thanks for each other and the holiday. We have inter-faith Thanksgiving service, inter-faith Memorial Day service, and inter-faith Independence Day service every year, and this is the pinnacle of religious cooperation and respect. My family celebrates Passover with the Rabbi’s family, and his family celebrates Christmas eve with mine. To say that religious groups cannot have positive interactions would be an absolute lie, because the key to interaction is open-mindedness.
chunks.label: Family's interfaith services and friendships
chunks.what_happened: The student participates in interfaith holiday services and family holiday celebrations shared with a local Rabbi, Imam, and Bhikkhuni through their minister father.
chunks.people: father, Rabbi, Imam, Bhikkhuni, family, Rabbi's family

chunks.text:
Using the answer to the previous two questions, we are able to get a better understanding of how religion impacts society. Because religion has been shown to increase individual life satisfaction and overall wellbeing, religion impacts the individual positively. Because of heightened religious tension, individuals find it more difficult to have positive interactions with people of other religious groups, but it isn’t hard if one keeps an open mind. Religion would have the best impact on society as a whole if everyone was a member of the same religious community, but that will never be the case. It is hard for many religions to admit that other people have valid reasons for believing what they do, and I think this is because of their own religious insecurity. While I think that it is very beneficial to practice religion for social and individual wellbeing, I find it problematic that there is no evidence to prove the validity of religion, it is all based on tradition. Religion keeps members under control by both fear and mercy, that they can mess up and be forgiven, but if they mess up too badly, they may be struck down by their heavenly figure (Köhrsen, 2012). Another problem with religion is that it just came out of nowhere one day. A person can get a lot of support if they claim that they were ordained by the gods, and many people have taken advantage of that for political power. According to Jaco Beyer, in the case of South Africa, religion and politics have a long history of reciprocal collaboration and/or disagreement (Beyer, 2015). From the earliest societies to present day, religion has had influence on politics. Beyer says that the sacred is present in social institutions, laws are divine commandments, social classes are arranged hierarchically as determined by divine order, education is religious, economic behavior is regulated by the sacred, government is sacral, and that religion and government is an integrated system (Beyer, 2015). A lot of this was seen in colonization, and in Beyer’s case, it was seen in both South Africa and Japan. Even nonreligious sociologists and psychologists seem to agree religion, when used correctly, is a vital part of society.

Because it answers difficult questions regarding life, death, struggles, and other topics, people tend to accept religious belief as truth and follow the other commandments and values of the given religion. Without religion, the world would be full of unmotivated people who are just waiting for death, knowing that life means nothing. Religion, when used incorrectly, has started the worst wars in history-- most wars have been the result of some kind of religious dispute that got out of hand, and this is part of what led Marx to say, “Religion is the opiate of the people.” While Marx argued that religion keeps people sedated and addicted, not even realizing how harmful it is, other people like Jens Köhrsen argued that religion is what enables people to do so many great things, such as giving to the poor, volunteering time to others, and caring about other people (Köhrsen, 2012). As I said earlier, when religion is used correctly, it is a beautiful piece of humanity that has many positive impacts on society. However, when it is used for political power or economic influence, its impact on society becomes negative. Religion is vital to a functioning society, and this can be seen in all of the ways I spoke about: Individual wellbeing, group interaction, and positive societal impact.
chunks.label: Sociological critique and concluding synthesis
chunks.what_happened: The student analyzes political and social dimensions of religion using sociological sources, weighing its negative misuses against its vital benefits to human life.
