chunks.what_happened: The student concludes by summarizing how outside influences force conformity to gender roles, while noting greater acceptance in today's generation.

n38bc3308.title: Navigating Female Competition and Body Standards

chunks.text:
How do you define beauty? There are many different ideas and views of what beauty is in society. You can look at any social media platform for example and see that there is a beauty standard that is in place, but the real question is, do you know who put these beauty standards in place? Men did. The reason that women feel the need to be beautiful even in today's society is because of men and how they viewed women in the earlier ages.

Women became subjected to the “beauty myth” back in the late 1800s because of men and their views on women. Back then the only use for women was to be a housewife to a man, and if they did not succeed at finding a husband they would most likely they would die. Women were unable to support themselves on their own back then because as you know it wasn’t until the early 1900’s that women gained the rights to own land and get jobs. Because of this, women felt like they needed to compete with others to gain the most attention from the men. The problem caused by this is a separation that was beginning to form between women everywhere. Everything was always a competition to them due to the view of the men.

This led women to believe that their value was based on their looks and how men viewed them rather than their personality, talents, and knowledge. The women who were not considered as beautiful as others by men then developed some-what of a fear towards the other women. We can understand this because women would be forced to compare themselves to others. This caused a lot of the competition we still see to this day between women in many different fields. If a woman is the face of a business she usually has stereotypical beauty standard features. This is because it is what the business knows will draw in the most people and make the most money.

A lot of the women who believed that they would not equate to anything because of their looks would develop mental disorders such as depression and anxiety. They would have to face this every day and have this constant feeling of judgment over them knowing that they would not be “good enough” for the men. Mental disorders then led to physical disorders such as anorexia and bulimia. Women would starve themselves or throw up their food just so that they would not gain weight. They would wear uncomfortable corsets and clothing that made their features more prominent all so that men would see them as “beautiful”. Women would go through all of these hardships just to please men, why? Because it is what they had to do to survive back then, but people today still show signs of this in a lot of different ways.

Although the world has gone through a lot of change since these times, the one thing that has not changed is the value of beauty to women and men. For example, in society as a woman, there are times that I feel threatened by other women because of their looks. As we have studied, sociologically a man’s brain is formed to look at women they find beautiful and turn away from the ones that they do not find beautiful. This impacts women’s everyday lives as they may feel that they have to impress people with their looks. Being a woman in society can cause a lot of pressure because of the ideals for women that men have kept up and even the new ones they have created.

We had this one discussion in class where we looked up attractive men versus attractive women. We noticed many differences between the pictures that showed up for each of them. The main differences were that there was more of a variety of men than there were of women and the men were wearing more professional clothes and expressions. While the women were wearing revealing clothing with more subtle submissive expressions. This shows that there are certain stereotypes forced into women’s heads for what “beautiful” is. This is because men have institutionalized their thoughts and ideas of “beautiful” women.

Another very clear modern-day example of this is shown throughout social media. When you post a picture of yourself do you post the worst one or the best one? Everyone posts their best photos in hope that people will be appealed to them. As we learned, the views that others have on us have a very high effect on the way that we perceive and look at ourselves. If someone comments on a picture that you posted saying something rude or vulgar then you are more than likely to either delete the comment or the picture. We do this because what other people say and do towards us either boosts or plummets our self-esteem. This is why we see people, especially famous women, posting only the very best photos of themselves.

Another very prominent yet concerning example is pornography. Pornography is one of the most money-making media productions to this day. Meaning, it gets a lot of viewers and reactions. This created another factor of the “beauty myth” that women now have to be worried about. This is another example of how men sexualized women by making them vulnerable to their sense of sexual self-worth. Because of this, women feel like they need to perform like the people they see when doing sexual things. This is such a bad thing that is being placed into women's heads all over the world today because of how much the media is portraying it. For example, I will e scrolling on my phone through Instagram and then randomly there is just a half-naked woman on my screen that is reposted by a page run by men. I have seen this happen to many other people as well. That just shows that men are trying to advertise women’s bodies to their own benefit.
chunks.label: Sociological reflection on beauty standards and male dominance
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on the historical and modern origins of the beauty myth, discussing how men's standards affect women's self-worth, social media dynamics, class discussions, and online sexualization.

chunks.text: For a more personal reflection, the idea of the “beauty myth” itself has caused many problems for women in the past and present. It affects the connections that women can form with each other. In my own experiences, almost every woman I have been friends with has either left or turned their back on me due to matters dealing with men. Therefore, I have a very hard time connecting with other women because I am afraid that they will begin to find something to compete about and cause problems. As for the men, I personally have seen the way that some men discuss women and their features. It is honestly insulting some of the ways that I have seen men just bring up women and sexualize them when there was not even a conversation going on about that. It is really harmful to people especially if they have insecurity’s, I would know because at the beginning of high school I was a bigger kid. I would see all of these skinny girls getting hit on by the guys and I would think “I am definitely not pretty enough for guys to talk to me like that.” That brought down my self-esteem and made me feel really self-conscious. At some point, I got tired of not looking like all of these other girls so I did something about it. Now I get referred to as “too skinny” or “anorexic”. It is as if there is always something for someone to say. People do not seem to understand that the way that they talk and the things that they talk about really do have an effect on the people they talk about.
chunks.label: Experiences with female friends, male comments, and body image
chunks.what_happened: The student experienced female friends turning on them over men, overheard men sexualizing women, and changed their body after feeling insecure about their weight in high school, only to be criticized for being too skinny.
chunks.feelings: afraid, insulting, brought down self-esteem, self-conscious, tired
chunks.people: female friends, men, guys, skinny girls, people

chunks.text:
Understanding the male brain is very hard. In sociology, we are taught that men feel the need to have this feeling of power over others called “Hegemonic Masculinity.” This is a dominant form of masculinity that tells men that they need to follow the stereotypical male traits. It explains why men feel the need to maintain dominance over women and others such as their jobs. As we discussed in class, there could possibly be a corollary “beauty myth” for men. When you think of masculinity what do you think of? Men are stereotypically supposed to be strong, be serious, have a good job that pays well, and providing for their beautiful wife and family. Therefore, most men probably have a feeling of fear and competition towards other men. Hence why they fight so hard for the most “beautiful” women and have so much pride when they do have one. But even with this in place, men still feel so dominant over women.

In conclusion, the way the world views women could have been very different if it were not for the views that men had and still have of women. Women have been degraded and undermined causing them to form many different problems and trials thought out their life because of the beauty standards that are put in place by men. Even in today’s society, women still have a fear of competition towards other women. If men were to focus more on the personality and knowledge of a woman rather than her looks and beauty that there would be much less tension between women. Everyone has some things that they are insecure about and being taught that you must be perfect can be very harmful to your well-being. Many women suffer from mental health issues and even physical health issues because of the way that media and men have portrayed the “beauty myth” in reality.
chunks.label: Sociological analysis of masculinity and concluding thoughts on beauty standards
chunks.what_happened: The student discusses sociological concepts like hegemonic masculinity and concludes on the negative mental and physical health impacts that male-driven beauty standards impose on women.

n4c5b5158.title: Reflecting on Interlocking Systems of Oppression

chunks.text: Collins argues that race, social class, and gender comprise interlocking systems of oppression or a “matrix of domination.” This goes deeper than just men dominating women, but that oppressed people have been dominated by others of higher “values.” Everything being more materialistic than humane to any person no matter what race, gender, or social class they are. Collins talks more on how gender equality is hard on women but even harder on women of color. Collins highlights the point that black women in a house are more likely to be emotionally or physically abused by their partner, which reflect practices that African American women are completely opposed to. Black female spheres of influence constitute potential sanctuaries where individual black women and men are nurtured in order to confront oppressive social institutions. These institutions help tie communities together while also being ran by African American women, a huge accomplishment in that area of feminism and growth for the black community.
chunks.label: Collins's matrix of domination and black feminist thought
chunks.what_happened: The student discusses Collins's theory on race, class, and gender as interlocking systems of oppression, as well as the unique struggles and community-building spheres of influence of black women.

chunks.text: These two readings correlate in the sense that feminism has grown to become a group of women who have changed how society views gender. The equality for women has grown tremendously and women can now express themselves the way they want and not feel dominated by men. Although this world has not become fully equal in terms of gender and race, it is evident that it has gotten better and will continue to grow.
chunks.label: Growth of feminism and progress toward gender equality

n0a4b9d6f.title: Examining Workplace Gender Inequality and Pay

chunks.text:
Unequal pay has been a tremendous issue in the workplace for many years and more than ever inequality between men and women in the workplace and is being noticed and changed. Throughout the centuries, gender is viewed as an accomplishment or an achieved aspiration for society because individuals can do their gender while working in society. For women working in the workplace, their gender may not always be done or noticed. Gender is a complex that is associated with not only biology but internal and external forces. Gender is a display of behavioral traits, which makes gender roles in society noticed and not easily changed. Often, we look past the unequal pay the workplace between men and women since gender is being displayed and people, like males, are doing their gender in society, and many women are unable to do so.

Looking at gender discrimination in the United States for women, a high percent of women in the United States have reported gender discrimination and multiple types of harassment by coworkers in multiple professions (Steelfisher Methods). Looking deeper into the data collected, 18 percent of women reported discrimination in health care settings, and 20 percent of women have reported discrimination in higher education settings (Steelfisher Principal Findings). This information leads to the conclusion that most women experience discrimination and harassment at some point in their lives, whether it is in the workplace or at a grocery store. This has an impact on the safety of women in the workplace as well as their overall health may decline due to these findings. A workplace should feel comfortable for the workers as well as the customers, or people will not be returning.

The evidence for this study conducted on 1596 women between the span of four months showed that gender discrimination impacted health of these women negatively as poor physical and mental health and increases blood pressure, stress on the body and heart disease (Steelfisher 1 Introduction). Questions were asked about discrimination in places such as housing, health care, police, courts as well as education and employment. The questions were geared towards violence, discrimination and avoiding specific institutions of the result of fear. Overall, the results summed up that women have reported violence and discrimination in areas outside of the workplace, for example, governmental institutions, health care, and higher education, which leads to negative impacts on physical and mental health. Addressing these issues to companies and corporations will bring this percentage down as well as make women feel safer in the places that they are supposed to feel safe in the first place.

Similarly, negative health outcomes due to higher stress caused by discrimination in the workplace will lead to physiological stress responses and a decrease in a successful performance with daily tasks in the workplace (Steelfisher Conclusions) to decrease this happened, specific steps need to be taken in order to change the discrimination in the workplace against women to zero percent. This can be done by workplaces teaching and addressing staff on how to treat each other in the workplace. Making this change, will not only help women feel comfortable in the workplace, but feel comfortable in their homes and doing daily activities. Education for this subject will need further improvements to make sure that discrimination against women, particularly those of racial and ethnic minority as well as LGBTQ, (Steelfisher Conclusions) to make sure the workplace in the United States stays comfortable for everyone. Bringing visibility to these issues will further the conversation and impact the careers at hand.

When it comes to understanding the pay for women and children it is mostly referred to the “Family Gap” (Waldfogel 1). This gap is directly related to women with children and without children in the workplace. The unequal gap between men and women is still noticeable however, this gap usually goes unnoticed because of the way it is explained and some find it difficult to understand. This has to do with maternity leave and how it raises women’s pay over childbirth. Over time, women’s’ wages compared to men have gone up due to women’s human capital rising and women have been increasing time and investment on education and less on the labor market or workforce (Waldfogel 2). Gender gap and the unequal pay between men and women may be rising due to the fact of the existing family gap in the United States, and it not being present in other countries (Waldfogel 4). It is known that there is a family gap present in the United States since there is a 10 to 15 percent penalty for women with children and women without children in the workplace based on education and work experience. As well as there is no family penalty for men, making this an even bigger issue to evaluate (Waldfogel 7). The cause of this gap comes from the fact that women with children and women without children have differences in full-time and part-time work experience as well as overall work experience and education for the job at hand. Discrimination against women with children in the workplace is also considered because women are not paid for maternity leave, and they may not have the time in the day to work long hours like women with no children. Overall, protecting maternity leave under the job will possibly raise women’s pay and then maintaining their job and benefitting from the specific human capital (Waldfogel 14). Women that are employed in larger firms in the United States will in turn receive maternity leave coverage, and that women are more likely to return to the same workplace after maternity leave, in turn raising women’s pay, wages will increase, and they will continue to work for that specific company. As we examine further in the differences between women with children and women without children working in the workplace, women with children will be paid less due to if they have maternity leave with the same employer as well as their time is not mainly focused on the work, like women without children; the time is between the woman and her children and the workplace, making less hours for the woman to work thus, getting paid less.

Dealing with equal work but an unequal pay status showing the United States that there is “gender equity in terms of workload but inequality in terms of pay and status” (Dobele 3). Universities dealing with unequal pay and a higher workload in the workplace, may lead to lawsuits and this is not always mentioned, however it is a serious issue that needs to be discussed. This study done between two Australian mid-tier universities, that focused on two areas, teaching responsibilities and the research output for the study (Dobele 6). Assessing to the gender imbalance in the workplace will not only improve the functions and responsibilities for the company or university but improve the quality of work being done and how fast it is being completed. The study showed that fewer women were employed in the senior rank jobs, and more males were seen present in those positions. With some positions in the workplace having the same workload, a person getting paid more for doing the same tasks should not be the case. Overall, the research concluded that the second University with more female staff than University 1, were less research based when compared to the second university. Both universities also had more women that were employed into the junior ranks than men. This shows that women are at an effect for being in junior ranked professions, with women exceeding for the Associated Professor and Professor ranks; the highest ranks, yet still paid less for the same amount of work (Dobele 7). This research and conclusion for this study is that unequal pay still exists even though some employees are working the same workload at a University or place of employment.

This could be the result of not many women being skilled in that specific field of work, (Dobele 10) however this number has been increasing due to women’s access to education increasing and the increasing interest in certain professions being available for women in the workplace. This is called the pipeline argument as explained by Dobele, and the explanation for the academic or university level gender gap is due to factors like family circumstances, or living situations, as well as social capital, work experience, education, the differing positions between researching and teaching the material at the University. Compared to men, women tend to switch careers or prefer part-time over a full-time workload. This has to do with personal choices, not related to the work environment itself.

In conclusion, there is a significant gap between the pay in the workplace between men and women based on the multiple studies done on the issue. With the three research studies, women with children are increasingly underpaid due to the maternity leave compared to women without children. The gender gap is present through multiple factors like family background, socioeconomic issues and gender inequality with wages. Each company handles their pay differently as well as their work schedule and work environment, however each company or University should be mandated to have equal pay between all co-workers including women with children and women without children, men in higher positions, and women in higher positions. This should be mandated through policy checks as well as mandated meetings on this issue to keep education present and each co-worker has knowledge of this issue. Helping close the wage gap will lead to everyone feeling safe and against discrimination in the workplace, making for a better work environment.
chunks.label: Research reflection on gender discrimination and unequal pay
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on academic studies regarding gender discrimination, health impacts, the family pay gap, maternity leave, and unequal pay in university settings, concluding with recommendations for workplace policy.

chunks.text:
The Difference Between Gender and Sex and How Social Media Impacts Mental Health

When a person feels as though they need to change their gender, it is because they do not feel right in their own body. There is a term for this which is, gender dysphoria. Gender dysphoria is distress due to a discrepancy between one’s assigned gender and gender identity. Adults who wish to access gender clinics are assessed to ensure they meet the diagnostic criteria for gender dysphoria. Therefore, the definition of gender dysphoria has a significant impact on the lives of individuals who wish to undergo physical gender transition. (Cooper, 2020) Since there is now more help available for people who struggle with gender dysphoria, we see an increase in people coming out to show who they really want to be. With these gender clinics, it makes it easier for people to help get the treatment for their transition, as well as allow people to find their inner peace. These clinics will allow people with gender dysphoria to have a safe place to talk about their insecurities and get on the right track for any necessary medical help. The clinics also support that some people might need a special place for treatment and realize that their gender is not correct with their sex. Gender diversity is not considered a mental health problem. However, transgender people are more likely to experience mental health problems than the general population. (Cooper, 2020) The clinics are not here to try and change how a person feels in their own body, it is for support. It is there to help a person become who they really feel on the inside and be comfortable in their own body. It is to prevent mental health issues and get their journey to transitioning quicker.

Stereotypes exist all over the internet, especially on social media. One bias is gender stereotyping, which refers to the practice of ascribing to an individual woman or man specific attributes, characteristics, or roles by reason only of her or his membership in the social group of women or men. However, gender stereotyping is a complex process that, although based on strong beliefs of what gender is and should be, is understood too simplistically. (Fosch-Villaronga, 2021) Having these stereotypes all over the internet can cause people to have a closed mind about gender and what the correct definition of gender is. As someone fills in their profile information, you come across, “what gender?” and the options are male or female. Fixed into the profile just made will either show more feminine or masculine products to fit that gender. Still, these stereotypes persist online and, as if platforms failed to understand—or deliberately choose to ignore—that gender is not merely being a ‘man’ or a ‘woman,’ but a social construct. In the words of De Beauvoir, “one is not born, but rather becomes a woman.” (Fosch-Villaronga, 2021) As people grow and learn their own behaviors and choose the gender they desire and feel so drawn to. Society now has to accept this concept and understand that not everyone feels the same about their sex as they do their gender. Since gender identity is primarily subjective and internal, it also clashes with the idea that gender can be recognized automatically, at least with the state of art gender classification systems (GCS). (Fosch-Villaronga, 2021) If someone is walking around dressed like a girl and using feminine mannerisms, it would be hard to tell if they are that sex and vice versa. Once people figure out that their gender is different from their sex, issues arise because some people still can’t wrap their head around the concept that gender is an internal feeling that someone cannot control.

Social media can be a harsh place for bullying, especially for people in the LGBTQ community. People who will express themselves freely may be seen as “abnormal” and not set to the social standard. This can affect the mental health of people within the community but also, with the growth of social media, more support is out there. Research suggests that online settings provide sexual and gender minorities with opportunities for exploration with identity presentation and disclosure that the specific affordance of particular settings shapes the experience and the possibilities for development. In addition, research suggests that the experience of online settings varies across subcommunities of gender and sexual minorities, as some online settings can be spaces in which intra-community stigma is enacted or intra-community tensions exacerbated. (Hammock, 2021) Social media is a source of help but also can be a source of hate since there is always two sides of opinions about gender identity. One side supports it and can understand that gender is not a set thing to a person and the other side would be the ones who cannot understand the concept that gender is internal and think they are just “ill.” Once you enter the supportive side of social media, it can create a safe place and become a source of help. People can also create friends that they never would have known without social media. These and other social media platforms created a new social context for interaction and the formation of communities and subcultures. (Hammock, 2021) With the communities and subcultures, a person with no support in their personal life can now obtain some. Finding people struggling with the same problems to talk and be close with will put down the numbers of mental health issues in transgender people and make them feel security and hope again.

With all these sources, they all have a common thread among them all. They all support and exchange the idea of gender being an internal feeling that cannot be changed. Dominant social narratives that gender identity and biological sex should align did not fit the transgender person, which resulted in conflict and sadness. This links to the earlier theme of confusion, whereby participants were unsettled by their gender identity not aligning with societal expectations. (Cooper, 2020) “Sex” usually refers to the assigned gender at birth based on medical factors (e.g. genitalia, chromosomes and hormones), usually ‘male’ or ‘female.’ “Gender” is both a “person’s internal, deeply held sense of their gender,” also called gender identity. —but is also tied to social, cultural and legal factors. (Fosch-Villaronga, 2021) With regard to gender identity, it is increasingly common to distinguish between cisgender (i.e., one’s current gender identity matches the sex assigned at birth) and transgender identities (i.e., one’s current gender identity is different from the sex assigned at birth.) (Hammock, 2021) These definitions from each article will all relate back to the reading from class “Doing Gender” and how West and Zimmerman had explicitly pointed out the two difference in sex and gender. Pointing these out in each section can support the claim that gender and sex are two very different things and gender can be interchangeable. With people being able to express themselves freely it shows other people that they can too. They can also share their stories through social media to support anyone struggling with coming out and being who they truly wish to be.

Social media in the mix of all of this is an important factor to if a person has support and their mental health state. There are many support groups through social media that allow people who have gender identity issues to reach out and gain information and support. Social media is also a huge platform that can support transgender people and get the word out that it is not merely a mental issue but a disorder that cannot be “cured.” With platforms being able to get out valid information it can help educate people to the issue, not to try and change them, but understand the concept of gender dysphoria and how it impacts someone’s everyday life.

In West and Zimmerman’s article “Doing Gender” the main purpose was to inform the readers about the differences in sex and gender. They thoroughly showed this through many examples and facts. They explain the theory that gender roles are learned and enacted by observing people through real life and this can also tie back to social media. Just by using social media each day, you see how people act and what certain genders do through these platforms. The females are usually influencers and then you have the males who work out or are doing more of a comedy thing. There is a very distinct line through male and female roles that can be adapted just by going through everyday life. With the increase of social media and younger generations being exposed earlier people can see an increase in the desire to show who they really are. Social media allows people to express themselves freely and while there can be hate and bullying there is a tremendous amount of support throughout all of the platforms including groups and even a hashtag.

Gender is a trait that can be changed if you feel as though it should be, and social media provides healthy support to anyone second guessing this. This is such a strong topic nowadays because we see that more and more people are coming out and showing who they really feel they are. Without the support of social media, the world may be very different today because not many people would have realized what their feeling is normal, and they should be embracing it and not hiding it. Gender dysphoria is not a mental health issue it is more of a disorder that someone cannot change. Instead of hiding it people should embrace it so that anyone feeling the same way as them can see it and be their true self.

Work cited

Cooper, K., Russell, A., Mandy, W., & Butler, C. (2020). The phenomenology of gender dysphoria in adults: A systematic review and meta-synthesis. Clinical Psychology Review, 80, 101875. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpr.2020.101875

Fosch-Villaronga, E., Poulsen, A., Søraa, R. A., & Custers, B. H. M. (2021). A little bird told me your gender: Gender inferences in social media. Information Processing & Management, 58(3), 102541. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ipm.2021.102541

Hammack, P. L., Hughes, S. D., Atwood, J. M., Cohen, E. M., & Clark, R. C. (2021). Gender and Sexual Identity in Adolescence: A Mixed-Methods Study of Labeling in Diverse Community Settings. Journal of Adolescent Research, 074355842110003. https://doi.org/10.1177/07435584211000315

In “21 Lessons for the 21st Century”, Noah explains this with an example of Mark Zuckerberg and the creation of Facebook. Human groups will traditionally have conflicts and disagreeing opinions based on every individual’s specific thoughts and feelings towards a subject. As humans we also have certain social groups that form out of unconscious thinking because that is how humans brain function and work. Human social groups are based on what is currently happening or what we make of it. It is defined by changes more than continuity. A quote from the text that can explain this would be, “No matter what revolutions they experience, they can usually weave old and new into a single yarn” (Noah 63) (PDF Version). This can describe civilization today because we rely on old and new ideas and opinions to create societal groups and work as one society, like yarn in a blanket, even though we are divided.

This concept can heavily relate to Mead’s essay, “The Self, the I, and the Me”. Within his writing he connects the collective consciousness to individualism and the self is a single entity living a in a world with other bodies. Humans communicate with different behaviors, expressions, emotions, and languages that it is universally indicated that humans have different opinions and are divided into different social groups within society. An individual experiences themselves indirectly through the expressions of others, because humans cannot see themselves as they interact in society. Communication is a big part in this because that behavior introduces the self into the world. A quote from the text that explains this idea about communication would be, “The unity and structure of the complete self reflects the unity and structure of the social process as a whole; and each of the elementary selves of which it is composed reflects the unity..., implicated” (Mead 165). This explains the concept of communication because we are all united through communication and agreeance in society. We are composed of our own ideas and beliefs which all blend together to develop societal views and opinions as whole.

Connecting this to civilization, each human on earth has different thoughts and feelings, as well as we are all individual selves living in a world of communication and rapid developing cultures and societies within one whole. Unity plays a big part in this as well because we all have duties as an individual in the world, living each on our own. This relates to our thoughts and feelings and that are opinions are mainly based on experiences. This is why humans naturally form societal groups that make up one society, because as humans, we cannot agree on one thing or concept of ideas.

Throughout life, labor and capitalism are an important topic when discussing how humans communicate with each other, as well as work in society together. With this comes the social hierarchy that is created through exchange values. This is where labor is stratified according to its specific value in society. This then ignores the social relations required to produce this specific commodity.

Something about modern life that makes sense to me would be the discussions featured Weber’s writing, “The Spirit of Capitalism”. This is because everyone in society is producing new ideas, new ways of thinking, and new problems to be solved. This is because of the rapid growth of society and how well people respond to their surroundings. When shown a specific object that everyone owns and has, people will be more likely to purchase the product due to the idea of conformity. A quote that can explain this would be, “No one knows who will live in this cage in the future, or whether at the end of this tremendous development entirely new prophets will arise, or there will be a great re-birth of old ideas and ideals” (Weber 2). Modern capitalism is seen as a re-birth of something new to make all the functions of different social groups work. Capitalism supports freedom, innovation and opportunity, however that can become a shadow behind conformity, because that is how society is socially structured.

n0da7495f.title: Analyzing Gender Norms on Social Media

chunks.text:
Why are most humans, who have access, compelled to share on social networks private information about themselves and why do they take others' information seriously? More importantly, why is it that members of social media sites internalize that which they do take seriously? Since its inception, social networking has amassed an exponentially increasing amount of active users who post, share, like, dislike, and comment about the small and large details and events in their and others’ lives. There are numerous platforms on which you can perform these functions. The one’s I will be discussing are Reddit, a platform which hosts communities that focus on particular topics for discussion and Instagram, which is less chat based and more for sharing pictures and videos. However, none of these sites are immune to the growing problem that has developed simultaneously with their popularity surge. The advantages of this new medium are apparent, you can remain in contact with distant relatives and friends, and find new friends who share your interests. While this new mode of online communication has spurred a new wave of global connectivity, by the same token, it created negative social cosnequences. These consequences are an integral part of the growing problem which is not solely inherent to the social media sites but is inherent to human interactions in society, something which the site reflects hyperbollically. In short, social media is a mirror that reflects how we interact with one another and the term hyperbolic represents the conflated fictitiousness that accompanies these reflections. While it serves as a window into our sociology, it also reflects the malignant social stereotypes that plague our society, make up our social customs, and permeate through our institutions. Social networking platforms hyperbolic reflection of our everyday interactions reinforces social stereotypes particularly where it pertains to gender in the offline world.

An incorretable flaw in the design of social media is that everyone is posting the highlights of their days, weeks or even months, which people erroneously assume to be their everyday life. If users' posts are devoid of the mundaness of life and viewers are incapable of realizing the difference between fact and fiction. They inevitably feel worse about themselves and may be compelled to fake their posts, the hyperbolic aspect, to communicate a sense of perfection in their lives as a way of competing against others. Posters do this to achieve validation and claim illusory feelings of happiness. To successfully compete against others in having the best, happiest, and most interesting lives installs them higher in the echelons of the social hierarchy. The method by which posters of this nature swear, collides with the satisfaction of gender norms and stereotypes. Likely, the reason for this is that the stereotypes are understandable, they are a cookie-cutter view of how a person should act and behave according to their gender. If these gender stereotypes embody the chracteriestic of a perfect human, fulfilling these standards provides posters with the simplest way to demonstrate perfection in their lives.

Erving Goffman, proposed that when we are born we are propelled onto a stage called life and our social interactions are formed by learning to play our roles from other people. When in the company of others we perform our role and they perform theirs for us too. I believe this concept supports my assertions regarding the reasons people post, take posts seriously, and box themselves into gender norms as a way to compete in the hirearchy. When one first creates their social media account it is akin to being born, as stated in the concept. The immediate online socialization begins to force the new user into a singular way of thinking, that being life demands perfection. Subsequently, they learn to replicate what is most common, the submission to gender norms as a means to propagate perfection. During this period is also when the user will have adequately prepared themselves to perform their role on the front stage. They post their content in competition with others and when finished they return to the back stage where reality sets in and they can step out of character. Context is important with Goffman’s stage theory, someone who socializes online will adapt their role differently than if they are socializing in person. Socializing for the poster is a context where reality is obscure and relative but for the offline communicator the personal connection mostly overcomes the online demand for perfection and submission to gender norms. This is an immutable facet of social networking, the design of these sites inadvertantly promotes competition between posters, which in turn demands their conformity to baseline standards which are socially desirable. It affects members of both genders and leads to the reinforcement of gender norms which supports gender inequaliy in society.

Social networks provide users with a social landscape wherein people can express themselves, their opinions, and feelings, likes, and dislikes. Self expression can be rewarding in that one can find a like minded person or crowd of people but by the same token it can invite criticism, harassment, or bullying. Such is the same in real life too, however an online setting concentrates its content for the user, you see what you want, unlike real life where what happens is largely arbitrary. Reddit for example has content partitioned into communities but they are largely dominated by gender affiliation. Reddit does not offer a diverse place to interact should you be interested in a topic which falls outside that which you would socially be expected to like based on gender. Statistically speaking, the communities with the highest percentage of female paticitpants are those that partake in quintessentially female things; Reddit reports that the most popular are makeup and fashion. Meanwhile, communities revolving around topics such as sports and video games have the highest percentage of male participants. This could be explained by a phenomenon whereby people group each other based on gender instead of topic or interest. Which is supported by the argument that the collective conscious furnishes our sense of self with a role to play according to our biological sex. Meaning, males will flock to tradionally masculine acitivities while females flock to feminine activities because their role requires it. Interestingly, topic categorization is further divided by gender using labels. Instead of there being a collective science community there is a subset for females interested in science, likewise, there is a female gamers subset instead of one for just gamers.

The nature of this labeling implies that the female domain is considered less than the male domain and that their interests must function depending on gender. It is as if there is an unspoken social rule where women should not join these communities because they are women. This concept of women being subordinate to males is reminiscent of the Woman as Other text by Simone Beauvoir. Beauvoir states that women are “other” because they live relative to men in society. There is not science but female science because they are the “second sex” and embody what men do not have. Member participation by gender in reddit communitites largly parallels real life gender norms. Males and females are segregated into their own communities based on gender stereotypes, which hinders diversity by and reinfroces exsiting notions of gender roles.

Apart from Reddit, which is primarily chat based, sites exist to share pictures and vidoes about yourself and your daily activities. Instagram, being one such site, allows users to share images of themselves. Many female users feel a societal pressure to doctor the images they post of themseleves in accordance with female standards of beauty. Apparently, 90% of young women in a recent study, reported using a filter or editing the physical appearance of themselves before posting their photo. Furthermore, the women in the study also reported that they regularly saw advertisements for cosmetic products or procedures to enhance their physical appearance. This data corroborates Naomi Wolf's concept of the beauty myth, which argues that women are pressured to conform to unrealistic beauty standards that results in them adopting unhealthy behaviors like a preoccupation with appearance.

Wolf’s beauty myth highlights the foundation on which many men view women and they view themselves. As well as fuel for the unfortunate cycle of young women getting exposed to advertisements which use beauty as a selling point, internalizing what they see and continuing to doctor their images, allowing cosmetic companies to take advantage of them. This feedback loop, as it is, powers the worsening mental health that can be observed in the younger generations that use social media by solidifying gender specific stereotypes.

Roles for humans to play according to their gender have existed for millenia and have adapted with time to the changing circumstances. In today’s world social media can be used as a tool to further understand the way gender norms impact our social interactions and way of thinking by peering into the fabric of our online interactions. It’s reflection of certain aspects of our sociology allows us necessary insight into the way social norms persist in society. Social media platforms like Reddit, passively enforce gender norms via the disparity in community statistics. Members organize themselves based on gender and not interests which yields undiverse and biased communities. Instagram, on the other hand, falls prey to the same architecture that runs networks, promoting conformity to gender norms through competion in a social hierarchy as a means to propagate a perfect online lifestyle. The architecture allows instagram advertisers to sell a lifestyle to vulnerable young women, which forces them to adhere to the beauty myth and down an unhealthy cycle of obsessing over their physical appearance. Since it forms the foundation upon which social networks are built, the architecture will continue to promote competition by hyperbollically reflecting our interactions and that inspires posters to conflate their own lives and post their own fictions consistent with the concept of gender norms.
chunks.label: Social media, gender norms, and sociological theories
chunks.what_happened: The student analyzes how social media platforms like Reddit and Instagram reflect and reinforce societal gender norms and stereotypes, connecting these dynamics to theories by Goffman, Beauvoir, and Wolf.

ncbba66b6.title: Watching a Twin Battle the Beauty Myth

chunks.text: Why are beauty standards so prevalent in our culture for women? What are these beauty standards or abstract ideas of beauty in regards to women? What are the dangers of these societal standards? Are men the perpetrators of these ideas, and if so, how should men in society respond? The beauty myth is a dangerous and flawed social concept that encompasses the idea that women should be judged and bound by their physical appearance. One does not have to look very far in modern society to see the ideal picture of a woman society paints. Popular culture, television, magazines, movies, and social media have had a substantial influence on the beauty myth, and have advanced the idea of beauty standards and expectations for women drastically. This phenomenon has led to an exponential rise in eating disorders, plastic surgery, anxiety, and depression. The power structure of society has a substantial role in the development and sustainment of the beauty myth. Men also must take ownership of this truth, if men have a role in the beauty standards that women feel, how much more responsibility do we have to combat the harmful ideology? Men must become active in fighting these beauty standards. Passivity among men in regards to these standards as well as advancement of them has led to substantial harm among women and even young girls.
chunks.label: Introduction to the beauty myth and society
chunks.what_happened: The student introduces the concept of the beauty myth, discussing how society, media, and men perpetuate harmful beauty standards that cause severe mental and physical harm to women.

chunks.text:
The beauty myth is a complex and substantial issue in modern society that must be acknowledged, addressed, and combated.

Female beauty standards and the beauty myth are something that I have not experienced directly as a man throughout my life, but I have experienced the dangers of these ideas deeply and personally through my family. It was a cold and snowy day on November 20th, 2002. That night at 9:37 PM, I experienced the light of this world for the first time. Eighteen minutes prior, my twin sister was born with a loud cry and tears of joy from my parents. Never in their wildest dreams did my parents ever think that they would have twins. Twins do not run in our family, and we were miracle children. We were born at 28 weeks weighing 2.2 and 2.8 pounds. Twins being born two months prematurely can be a very complicated and complex situation. We were immediately rushed to the NICU where we resided for six weeks after our birth. I am told that my sister and I were practically inseparable in the weeks following our arrival on this earth. I never cease to be fascinated when thinking about this fact. We were not even supposed to be born at that point, yet our bond was already so strong. The connection of twins is almost inexplicable. Growing up, we always were bombarded with twin telepathy jokes and banter. Obviously I was never able to look at my sister with x-ray vision and read her thoughts, but in some ways there is some truth to that old joke. Growing up we had a bond like nothing I have ever experienced. We did everything together, shared everything, and walked through early life together. She was all I ever knew and the closest person to me, and still is to this day. Looking back at our childhood I remember the Barbie dolls and makeup she would play with. It is very intriguing to be twenty years older and wiser and reflect on things I never could have noticed back then. Every Barbie doll had the same figure, the same blonde hair which my sister did not have, and reflected the images on the covers of magazines. In hindsight, I now am able to see the damage that those images had in my sister's mind. In no way am I claiming that Barbie Dolls are inherently evil, but I am raising an eyebrow at the ideology behind the cookie cutter nature of these dolls and the intent of the institutions that were responsible for the portrayal of the “ideal” female figure.
chunks.label: Birth and childhood bond with twin sister
chunks.what_happened: The student recounts being born prematurely as twins with his sister, their close bond while growing up, and observing her play with Barbie dolls that promoted uniform beauty standards.

chunks.text: When my sister and I were about 5 years old, we decided to each pick out some hobbies we wanted to try. I grew up playing piano and music was just my passion, but I wanted to try baseball and see if I enjoyed sports. My sister chose dance to try. Madison was born to dance. Dance is a part of her, it lives within her and is her way of expressing everything. The two of us are very passionate individuals. As we grew up, all each of us thought about were baseball and dance respectively. Baseball became a huge part of my identity. Dance became a substantial part of hers. She was just simply a dancer. She danced all day and dreamed of dancing on the big stage in front of thousands of people. Dance was her passion. As we grew into our pre teen years, dance became extremely competitive and challenging for her. The routines themselves were always an easy task for Madison, the real challenges of the dance world were tackling the intense social atmosphere of it. I remember being twelve years old and noticing the harsh environment and the intense nature of the dance world. I would even have conversations with my mom about how intense everything seemed. Within this competitive world of dance, body image is an enormous deal. Every dancer was pushed and prodded to look a certain way, act a certain way, have a skinny figure but not too skinny because that wouldn’t be pretty, but if you’re not skinny you will never win. Comparison ran rampant throughout this world and especially among the young girls who did not know any better. Week in and week out, competition after competition my sister was tangibly judged by paid judges on how good she looked, if she fit the mold, and if her dancing ability was good enough. Twelve year old girls were being told that they were not good enough, not skinny enough, not flexible enough, and just plain not good enough by grown adults who were getting paid to do so. I often questioned this toxic culture but accepted it as reality at that young age. In the fall of 2017, we began to notice changes in my sister. She slowly began to stop eating and was hyper focused on how she looked. At first we did not know what to think of this. She was an eighth grade girl so her struggles and insecurities were not abnormal. This trend continued for about a month and my family and I began to seriously worry. From this point on my sister began to take a drastic turn for the worst. She completely stopped eating and refused food. She would do sit-ups in the bathroom when no one was watching until one of us found her. She would sneak in the bathroom and constantly look at her body in the mirror, hating the beautiful girl she saw. She was diagnosed with anorexia in October of 2017. This wreaked havoc on our family. My mom and dad did not know what to do. I had no clue how to process this as an eighth grade boy. Our relatives did not understand the situation at all and dismissed it. Our family was almost ripped apart from the inside out. My sister continued to suffer from anorexia until she reached a breaking point on Christmas Eve that year. She has gone from 125 pounds to 92 in the span of about 3 months. She was also battling severe depression and anxiety and was admitted to the hospital on Christmas Eve. I remember that day as one of the darkest of my life. My family and I were lost and felt helpless, we were heartbroken and distraught. My sister was about a week away from death that day, her vital organs were suffering greatly and had begun to fail. Thankfully, that day is the lowest part of her story. From this point on, she began to heal and recover from her condition. Slowly and steadily, she improved and as a family we worked together to heal collectively. Madison’s story is not a story of defeat and trauma and pain, but a story of victory and strength. A story of triumph and overcoming a dark and painful situation. She still battles with body image issues today but has claimed victory over the war. She is happy and healthy and currently dancing at High Point University, pursuing her passion of dance.
chunks.label: Sister's dance career and battle with anorexia
chunks.what_happened: The student's twin sister pursued competitive dance, where intense pressure over body image led to her severe anorexia and hospitalization in eighth grade before she eventually recovered.
chunks.people: twin sister (Madison), mother, father, relatives, dance judges, teammates

chunks.text: The beauty myth is an issue discussed by Naomi Wolf in her writings. She discusses the concept and goes into depth about the issues surrounding this social ideology. The beauty myth is the social concept that women are supposed to look a certain way, act a certain way, and participate in select roles dictated by the power structure that encompasses them. Wolf discusses that the beauty myth and the concept of body images are tools that the institutions of society use to restrict women and keep power over them. By advancing the idea of beauty standards and that all women should look a certain way, act a certain way, and take certain roles, powerful institutions can keep a tight grip on women and keep them in positions where they cannot take their power away. Men also have a strong role I believe in the advancement of the beauty myth.
chunks.label: Naomi Wolf's concept of the beauty myth
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on Naomi Wolf's writings regarding the beauty myth and how societal institutions use beauty standards to restrict and control women.

chunks.text: I grew up in a baseball dugout my whole life and grew up around other teenage boys. In my experience, many boys and even grown men I knew and were around discussed women as objects and tools to use for pleasure and as trophies. My teammates and even coaches often discussed women only in sexual terms, making comments about the crude things that would want to do to women and how if some women didn’t fit this specific mold, they were worthless. I have experienced the dangers of this first hand in my life and feel a strong pull as a man myself to change this narrative. Men must take ownership of this problem and have accountability in facing it. The way we discuss women, treat women, date women, and judge women must change and must be done with respect and acknowledgment of the equality and value of women.
chunks.label: Witnessing toxic attitudes toward women in baseball
chunks.what_happened: Growing up playing baseball, the student observed teammates and coaches objectifying women and speaking about them in crude, degrading terms, prompting his call for male accountability.

chunks.text: In conclusion, the beauty myth is a dangerous and harmful ideology that many women sadly battle in modern society. Through social media outlets, entertainment, news, and many other forms of media women are portrayed as objects. Women are held captive to the lie that they have to look a certain way to have value. This lie has very severe consequences and ramifications in society and in the lives of women and young women. Action must be taken to combat this and men must take accountability and ownership of this problem. As a society, we must be good stewards of those who participate in society, and fight for justice, equality, and freedom from the bondage of beauty standards.
chunks.label: Conclusion on dismantling the beauty myth
chunks.what_happened: The student concludes by reiterating the harmful impacts of beauty standards portrayed by media and calling on men and society to fight for justice, equality, and change.

chunks.text:
Essay Brief 1 – The Evolutionary Origins of Social Consciousness

Over the past few millennia, humanity has been able to accomplish some truly amazing things, including inventing verbal and written language, building technological replicas of the human brains, and even figuring out that the speck of cosmic dust called earth actually orbits around a very large ball of gas and fire. But humanity owes all of our accomplishments to the formation of collective social consciousness and the beginning of social groups and civilizations where the collective consciousness could flourish. But when did these developments start and why?

Like anything else, all sociological ideas strong bases to hold themselves up. Fligstein and MacAdams call these bases microfoundations. As far as many sociologists can tell, the collective consciousness started to form roughly 50,000 years which were quickly followed by relics from undefined religious practices, such as burial. These two things were fueled by the advancing development of the neocortex in the brain as Maryanski and Turner describe in The Neurology of Religion. Because the collective consciousness is the source of groups in religion, it makes sense that the two developments in humanity coincide in the timeline. Maryanski and Turner make the point that not only was religion created for more practical reasons of helping a group stay together under a great sense being other than their animal themselves but it was created for safety proposes. The world is a very terrifying place and it is that fact as well as other parts to mirofoundations that fueled the need for sets of rules and beliefs.

They study of mircofoundations provides a clear light for sociologists to discover more about the psychological and situational events that lead to the development of religion and ancient societies. The fact that the development of mirofoundations was marked with relics that are now recognized as religious, in the broad sense, describes just how much humanity needed to feel like they were in control. All of the societal progress that humanity has witnessed over the past 50,000 years will always be thanks to the development of the collective conscious.
chunks.label: Evolutionary origins of social consciousness
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on the evolutionary origins of collective social consciousness, citing sociological concepts like microfoundations and neurology to explain the development of religion and society.

ncd4b0405.title: Societal Pressures of the Beauty Myth

chunks.text:
What is the beauty myth and how is it still used?

The beauty myth has been prevalent for centuries and has been researched for a long time. Where the beauty myth came from has not been acknowledged or studied, due to this, we will probably never have a hypothesis on that. However, we will be discussing how it is still used in society today. We will also discuss how it has affected society throughout the years. Our hope with this essay is to get an in-depth look at the beauty myth and where it stands today.

Before we get a perspective into how it has affected society, particularly women in society, we will take this chance to describe the beauty myth. The beauty myth according to our notes, is a societal standard affecting behavior towards women. This societal standard is where a woman is judged by her beauty, therefore, measuring her self-worth. This is also where aging is considered the enemy to this societal standard within the beauty myth. It also undid feminism practices in place at the time. The beauty myth, however, does not have a set time that it had developed even though it has been prevalent for centuries. It has been around for centuries with evolving and changing factors with no real source to the beauty myths origin.

Why is it that more women throughout history have been subjected to this beauty myth? I will give the reader a perspective on the women subjected to the beauty myth. According to our notes, these women have experienced pressure to conform to an unrealistic beauty standard deemed beautiful by society. There were also influences all around them through media and backlash against political progress. Society, specifically men, were threatened by more roles being created for women in their community. Socially constructed beauty was on the rise as was consumerism, beauty was seen as a commodity, and women were seen as objects.

Within society, there have been many instances of the beauty myth, and much research has been done on the beauty myth. First, we will talk about past research regarding the beauty myth. According to Susan Averett, a journalist with the Journal of Human Science in 1996, they “investigate income, marital status, and hourly pay differentials by body mass (kg/m2) in a sample of 23- to 31-year-olds drawn from the 1988 NLSY”. They have used this research to show that “obese women have lower family incomes than women whose weight-for-height is in the "recommended" range “. This is an example of how the beauty myth has affected society. It shows the difference that these beauty standards make between the weight classes in our society. The article also shows that “there is some evidence of labor market discrimination against obese women”.

This article shows the effect the beauty myth had on teens in the late 80s stating that “ Eating disorders (such as anorexia nervosa and bulimia) is a major social problem in the United States” having estimates such as ranges of “1 to 4 percent of the female population” for anorexia nervosa. There have also been higher estimates for bulimia nervosa “as high as 20 percent of college and high school females”. These implications a hard to ignore as they affect society's youth in extremely difficult ways.

One of the most frequent post-feminist beauty myths is a social media trend that happened in 2021 that is called “Strong is the new skinny” according to Jessica Maddox with the Feminist Media Studies. According to the article, “given postfeminist contradictions, this presents a terrain in which only certain women are even allowed to attempt to achieve the unobtainable body”. This trend gives a new face to the beauty myth and can be just as destructive as the beauty myth that started it all. This social media trend “repackages old body stereotypes in a way befitting the era of postfeminist confidence”. There has been a re-emergence of beauty myths located within social media trends. However, as stated in the article, some of these trends are “worth noting as feminism turns to the fourth wave and emphasizes hashtags-hashtags can turn and remain rhetorical if not critically probed”.

As we’ve discussed the beauty myth in this paper, we have gotten a deeper look into how it affects us as a society. Whether it be social media trends, eating disorders, or incomes it can affect us all. It is a societal standard that is prevalent in the past and today that can control how we think about ourselves and how we act in society. It is a long-standing standard that needs to change and can be very detrimental to mental health. Hopefully, in the future the beauty myth will be irrelevant to society.

Averett, S., and S. Korenman. "The Economic Reality of the Beauty Myth." The Journal of Human Resources, vol. 31, no. 2, 1996, pp. 304-330.

Maddox, Jessica. ""be a Badass with a Good Ass": Race, Freakery, and Postfeminism in the #StrongIsTheNewSkinny Beauty Myth." Feminist Media Studies, vol. 21, no. 2, 2021, pp. 211-232.
chunks.label: The beauty myth and its societal impacts
chunks.what_happened: The student discusses the concept of the beauty myth, reviews past research and modern social media trends related to body standards, and reflects on its detrimental impacts on women and society.

chunks.text:
Everyone associates different topics based off prior experience which leads to our categorizing it. This is how all living creatures learn and adapt to different situations that they are placed in, so they know how to appropriately respond. When individuals start to share similar mindsets and express them in an environment it creates a collective conscious which puts pressure on other individuals in that same environment. This is collective conscious and experience within it are prevalent for college students when they are deciding on what fields they want to enter. The environment, daily life, and interest in the field are factors that are all considered and create their own collective conscious within each discipline which will attract similar minded people. Another factor that is not talked about as much is gender, which most noticeably different among the science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) fields. This paper looks to explain why a disproportionate number of men enter the STEM fields compared to their female counterpart as a result of the collective conscious, difference in exposure prior to college, and different responses to classes. These factors make it so women wanting to enter a male dominated field become more difficult due to a cycle that has lasted generations.

The very first topic that was discussed in this sociology class was about the social consciousness and becoming aware of societies form. One author that elaborated on this was Emile Durkheim, who said that the collective conscious was formed from multiple people having the same values and ideas. The collective conscious this society formed could be viewed differently by other societies which means that a society can never be “correct”. It also puts a pressure on individuals that exist in it to conform to beliefs or methods practiced which may cause that individual to stray away from their true nature.

This concept is applicable in the college collective conscious for when people decide which field they wish to spend their life working or researching in, especially in STEM. Getting a degree is seen as a necessity to get a successful future within modern society so more people are inclined to go to college than in previous generations. With the STEM fields being notoriously hard for people, poor grades are bound to happen eventually for the majority of those who choose to go down that path. One area that was studied was the response to failing grades in men compared to women. This study found that women were more likely to change their major from a male dominated STEM field compared to men, who were more inclined to still pursue that same major (Kugler, 2021). They also found that women in male dominated STEM fields were more critical and harsher of their grades which was a big influence for switching majors. The reason for more women switching their major more frequently was denoted to the fact that because it was already male dominated, they might not matchup with the field even if they were to graduate where men did not have this concern.

The knowledge of the field being male dominated made enough of an impact to dictate decisions on whether to give up, which is completely external of the individual. Just because a person fails an exam or class in their major does not mean that they would be a terrible fit for it as a career. Their value and what they can contribute goes beyond what a test says and should be better elaborated in the STEM fields. These women who change their majors could be seen as falling under the pressure of the modern collective conscious to some extent by choosing to conform to more traditional female fields. Some of these women might have a talent for the field if they were to explore it more, but the collective conscious goes against them their entire journey by telling them they are social deviants. In some instances, they might even be told by their peers that they should leave the male dominated field because a woman has no place in it.

This trend of male dominated STEM fields can appear strange considering more women attend education institutions past high school. The common factor that most college students have is that they went to high school, which also influences career paths for many. With gender roles and beliefs existing in societies, high schools may limit the exposure of the STEM fields to women compared to men. Things such as clubs and elective classes also influence interests that last long term and can even turn into careers, so gender segregation outside the classroom also adds another reason for why men are pushed further towards STEM fields. Gender segregation starts early in society with kids being told by others what they are supposed to like due to their sex, which pushes them toward a certain direction in the future when they want to explore more options. By the time they reach high school they have been pushed far enough a certain way by parents, peers, and society that all the available options are not considered (Lewgie & DiPrete, 2014).

This early gender segregation of interests leads genders down a path that the collective conscious tells them is ok for them to be interested and work in, rather than letting the individuality of each person shine through. This pressure that each person faces throughout life alters the individual to fit more of what society wants or expects from them, keeping them trapped in a cyclic collective conscious. Societies are made and structured so that they are not easily changeable because most of the people in it create the rules, and if a person does not follow them then they are socially deviant. While everyone is socially deviant to an extent, there are core values integrated in societies that have harsher punishments compared to others. The punishment in this case would affect social life through school which would then transitions into work life after.

The other side of this trend in STEM fields falls on the side of the men. Questions may be asked about why they would be drawn to STEM rather than other fields of study. One study done found that men are more naturally inclined to gravitate toward STEM compared to women at all levels of high school math proficiency (Mann & DiPrete, 2013). While both men and women were close among math and science levels in high school, more men chose to enter a STEM field when they got to college partially due to life goals which was surveyed. Another factor to be noted in this study was that on average women had higher verbal and communication skills, which is also another contributor to women branching out more towards non-STEM fields. There are a lot of other reasons why people choose to pursue one major over the other, whether it be what they want their future to look like, money, or even stereotypes about that field. All these factors cannot be monitored and taken into account each study, but correlations can be drawn from quantitative data that is observable.

The impact the collective conscious played in this study was noticing that women were better at the communication and writing compared to men. If they feel they are good at something other people might not be as good at, they might be more inclined to go towards that direction to help benefit the overall society that the collective conscious puts pressure on. With some of these fields such as education, psychology, and fine arts being female dominated, more women may feel comfortable sticking in these fields and ok with the gender disparities. Having already late to no exposure to non-required classes in high school was also seen across all these studies, and another reason for not wanting to explore these fields due to stereotypes along with them.

The mindset people have when it comes to picking careers also comes with stereotypes of how people in that society perceive that career. The opinions of those around them also would influence their decisions while in post-secondary education. The collective conscious puts images and beliefs into its society from the experiences of others which generate stereotypes. These stereotypes are not based off fact, but rather opinions that were created and accepted by others to generalize. Stereotypes in the case of gender roles are harmful because they limit a person’s mindset and put forth false information that look to keep traditional values even if they are harmful. The stereotyping in STEM can seem like the fields are gatekept in a way. More men have reportedly wanted to keep the STEM field traditional compared to women who also say there is more injustice done towards them because of their gender (Castaño, Lubiano & García-Izquierdo, 2020). With more women feeling something is wrong with the collective conscious and stereotypes for them, they are considered social deviants as they are in the minority of what the STEM collective conscious views as acceptable. With men setting this collective conscious, they have set the impression and stereotype throughout the rest of society and a larger collective conscious that STEM is for males.

Breaking out of this collective conscious cycle is no easy feat, considering it still exists today just as it has in the past. The society is the one that changes and sets the collective conscious so all generations within it must widely accept it. This change cannot happen overnight but incorporating social deviance slowly would be an effective method that would slowly break apart these stereotypes and lack of exposure in society today. Education in modern society has been pushed more than ever before, so all paths should feel open to those who wish to continue past high school. Asian society however is completely different than American society in the fact that they encourage more people to pursue education in STEM regardless of gender. They also have seen results that research conducted among the same gender is more productive than if the two were opposite genders (Yang & Shen, 2020). This research also mentions the idea that female educators in STEM are seen as role models and encourage the younger female generations to enter STEM fields. This implies that if The United States were to hire more female STEM teachers, that over time more women would enter the field and push future generations to do the same. This would help break the collective conscious that is built in America and be more inviting towards women who might have an interest in STEM but are told that they should not pursue it because of their gender.

The impact that the collective conscious has is what drives a society whether it be seen as helpful or a hinderance. It wants to punish social deviance and reward conformity towards what is seen as acceptable, and with men deciding the collective conscious among STEM fields it allows them to keep these fields male dominated. As a result of this image women do not get the exposure throughout high school and childhood that men do to the STEM fields, which allows this to continue from generation to generation. This process will continue to exist until stereotypes and beliefs about women in STEM change to be more accepting of them which will in turn allow more exposure at younger ages to consider a STEM career path. With more gender equality and involvement in the STEM there can only be progression in the field as a result, which should not be feared by society. Encouragement should be done for anyone expressing interest in STEM just as it is in China. Breaking gender stereotypes created by the collective conscious must also be destroyed the same way by making this current deviance the accepted for the future. Societies are constantly looking to improve themselves through the lens of the collective conscious and making things deviant, but sometimes what is considered deviant is what is needed to improve.
chunks.label: Collective consciousness and gender disparities in STEM
chunks.what_happened: The student discusses sociological theories including Durkheim's collective conscious, reviews studies on gender segregation and stereotypes, and reflects on why women are underrepresented in STEM fields.

nb1188bd0.title: Examining Systemic Racism and White Privilege

chunks.text:
Racism, Sexism, Homophobia, Ageism, etc.; these issues are and have been incredibly prevalent in society since before recorded history because of the us versus them dynamic, which is one that most people fall into when talking about groups or cultures different from their own.
