chunks.what_happened: As a section leader, the student adhered to the rule of never letting junior Marines see leaders eat or sleep until all subordinates were fed, resting, or awake.

chunks.text:
This is important to take note of because as we discussed in class a collective consciousness is formed anytime humans interact in some pattern over time and many of the aspects which form the Marine Corps’ collective consciousness oppose what would be considered the status quo in the civilian population. In summary the fleet is where you become “a true killer”, it is where you learn the Marine Corps ethos of running towards the sound of gunfire, and caring for the life of your fellow Marine more than your own life.

There is a reason the Marine Corps is called a cult. We raise our idols to god hood, we have many traditions and methods which seem extreme, and our mentality seems a bit frightening, but these are all social and mental adaptations of a collective consciousness belonging to a culture whose job is to fight and often die on the orders handed down to them. This is why coming back to normal life after being completely reprogramed is an incredibly difficult task for most Marines whether they experienced combat or not (Doruk, 2008). They have essentially left behind their original collective consciousness and had a new one shoved into them only to have to transition back on their own once they re-enter normal life. However, that Marine Corps collective consciousness never truly leaves.
chunks.label: Difficulties of reintegrating into civilian society
chunks.what_happened: The student discusses how the intense collective consciousness that makes Marines effective also causes significant difficulty when transitioning back to civilian life.

chunks.text: For myself, I struggled with adjustment disorder and culture shock upon re entering civilian life. I still hold my morbid sense of humor which many of us adapt as a coping mechanism as well as a higher tolerance to stress.
chunks.label: Struggles transitioning to civilian life
chunks.what_happened: After leaving the service, the student experienced adjustment disorder, culture shock, and retained a morbid sense of humor and heightened stress tolerance.

chunks.text: All in all, the Marine Corps is unique among the American military because of the indoctrination into its own collective consciousness. While this occurs in other branches to a degree, it is not comparable to the level which it does for the Marines.
chunks.label: Concluding thoughts on Marine indoctrination
chunks.what_happened: The student concludes that the Marine Corps' indoctrination into a distinct collective consciousness is unmatched by any other military branch.

chunks.text:
How Television and Social Media Re-Define What It Means to Be Beautiful

Rebecca Walker

Department of Sociology, University of North Carolina Wilmington

Sociology 105-002

Professor Christopher S. Elliott

April 28th, 2021

In today’s society, body image has become a very sensitive topic. Instead of bringing women together, it has driven them farther and farther apart. Growing up, girls often don’t think about how their body looks compared to others until they start puberty. With everyone experiencing puberty at different times and speeds, it can cause girls to develop insecurities with their bodies. As they are exposed to television, they see many different body types and start to compare themselves to them. This holds true for teenagers and adult women as well because once they outgrow Disney Channel and Nickelodeon, they are exposed to channels and shows that depict the female body in its rawest from. As they see this, they also see adult men who seem to only be attracted to women with slimmer and curvier figures. This holds true with pornography as well because the most popular adult actresses are the skinnier women with “perfect” vaginas. This causes small flaws to stick out even more in a woman’s mind. They start questioning their own beauty and whether or not they amount to anything compared to these perfect models. Naturally, everyone wants to fit in, no one wants to be considered ugly or unattractive by society, but by making the beauty standards so specific it makes it hard to really embrace body positivity. Everywhere you go, you are more likely to see the skinny and “perfect” women, but do you ever stop to question how they got that way? A lot of celebrities including Taylor Swift, Lana Condor, Kesha, Paula Abdul, Demi Lovato, Candance Bure, and many others have struggled with different kinds of eating disorders. They have told their stories and it has allowed others to tell their stories as well in order to bring awareness to how important it is to love yourself and be who you are without feeling the need to change.

Sociologist Charles Cooley believes that individuals develop their self-image by observing how they are perceived by the other people around them. Cooley has referred to this concept as “the looking-glass self” and in today’s society, it is affected even more by the implications of television and social media. As women in particular start to determine their self-worth, it becomes heavily reliant on how people around them see them compared to how they see others. As they take into account what they see around them, they use it as a mirror to measure their value in relation to others. While some people are able to see themselves for who they truly are, for others it’s like looking through a fun house mirror. All of their flaws are distorted to the extremes and they start hating themselves for it.

Perceptions of what is considered attractive varies across different cultural groups especially for the female body size and shape. Based on the way our brains encode bodies and faces, just by altering what adults are exposed to, you can manipulate their attraction preferences. Historically in European art, the depictions of the female body shape remained the same throughout the classical and medieval area but switched to preferring a curvier body type during the modern era due to shape-altering undergarments (Boothroyd et al. 2020). To what extent are the perceptions of the female body really affected by television consumption? An article from the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology titled “Television Consumption Drives Perceptions of Female Body Attractiveness in a Population Undergoing Technological Transition”, really puts things into perspective. The authors conducted their research and experiments in a remote region of Nicaragua by sampling from villages who had different levels of access to television. Their studies concluded that participants in the low television access villages showed a stronger preference for larger body types than those in the high television access villages. It was also discovered that the control samples that were taken from the capital, Managua, preferred the thinnest body types of all of the recorded samples. This data alone shows how much television and media consumption can re-define beauty in a group of people.

How does this new definition of beauty affect women? Every woman’s body is different than another’s. While the new beauty standards may be in favor of some women, it is also not in favor of others. As stated in an article titled, “Risk Factors That Predict Future Onset of Each DSM-5 Eating Disorder: Predictive Specificity in High-Risk Adolescent Females”, from the Journal of Abnormal Psychology, women’s pursuit of the thin beauty ideal can result in body dissatisfaction/dysmorphia, and this causes some women to start binge eating and participating in other unhealthy weight control behaviors that could lead to anorexia or bulimia (Stice, Gau, Rohde, & Shaw 2017). These eating disorders affect 13% of females and even create a higher risk for future obesity, depression, suicide, and substance abuse. If a woman has one eating disorder, she is at an extremely high risk to develop another, they literally stack up and continue to get worse. These are the demons that some women end up dealing for their entire lives. The sad part is, a lot of them don’t even recognize that they need help, they are living their lives thinking what they are doing is natural and necessary. A good example of this would be YouTube star Eugenia Cooney. She has been posting on her channel since 2013, she has severe anorexia and almost looks she’s skin and bones. She never really opened up about her disorder and she’s posted regular videos. People often accused her of promoting her lifestyle but in recent news’s she has stated that she has been struggling for a long time and is working on getting help as she enters her late 20’s. Instead of attacking women, we should be doing everything we can to help them realize that they need help, it took way too long but she’s in rehab and getting the help she needs. There are still people suffering in their homes away from society dealing with this as well. They don’t see people all the time that can encourage them to be better. If they care enough all they have is social media. So in order to save the people we can’t even see we need to work together to help create a better more inclusive body positive content for those who don’t feel as represented.

Despite how it may seem, some advancements have been made in the right direction on social media. Body-positive posts on social media aim to challenge mainstream beauty ideals and encourage the acceptance and love of all female body types. How much has it really been able to do? An article titled, “#BoPo on Instagram: An experimental investigation of the effects of viewing body positive content on young women's mood and body image”, from the Journal of New Media and Society aimed to investigate the effect of viewing body-positive social media posts. One hundred ninety five young women, ages eighteen to thirty years old were randomly chosen to view either body-positive, thin-ideal, or appearance-neutral social media posts. The results showed that brief the women who were exposed to body positive posts exhibited an overall positive mood, body satisfaction and body appreciation, relative to thin-ideal and appearance-neutral posts. With that being said, both thin-ideal and body-positive posts were associated with increased self-objectification (Cohen, Fardouly, Newton-John, & Slater 2019). The women who were exposed to the skinny models, began reflecting on themselves and comparing themselves to the models, thus resulting in in dissatisfaction with their own bodies. Like Boothroyd discusses in her article about eating disorders, this negative image can lead to the development of increased self-objectification, body dissatisfaction, and disordered eating behaviors in women. However, with social media being filled with user-generated content, it allows for bodies that don’t exactly fit into the beauty standards to finally have a voice and be seen by the public. With this in mind, it allows for body-positive content to become really popular. As of April 28th, 2021 on Instagram #bodypositivity has 7.5 million posts compared to the 1.8 million reported in June of 2018 by the authors of this article. That growth that has been made over the course of 3 years is honestly amazing. In order to improve body appreciation researchers have stated that it is extremely important to provide women with broader conceptualizations of beauty and to encourage women to surround themselves with social networks that encourage women to appreciate their own body (Cohen, Fardouly, Newton-John, & Slater 2019). In the present study, women have been captioning their #bodypositivity posts with statements like ‘I am beautiful’, ‘I am beautiful despite my flaws’, ‘I am beautiful on the inside and out’. These statements are a clear indication of the women actually adopting a broader sense of beauty to incorporate a variety of appearances and attributes. These women are looking at the other women around them and instead of hating themselves, they are looking at it from a new view, a new view that speaks the truth, every body is beautiful, even your own.

Body image isn’t something that’s just a problem among women, men go through their own struggles as well, it’s just usually not on the surface. While women are liked regardless of height, if a man is shorter than a woman, she usually won’t give him a second look. There are always exceptions, but this is something that’s extremely common and shouldn’t be overlooked. Other than height, men have just as many things as women to be insecure about. So, while we are preaching #bodypositivity make sure everyone is included. Charles Cooley’s looking glass self can really be viewed at in many different ways. A person’s self-online is going to be different based on the website that they are on. A person’s profile on LinkedIn is going to present them in a completely different way than their Instagram or Twitter might present them. Despite this persona being purely online, it still translates to the real world, they can never escape possible judgement and criticism. As a person develops what is considered their cyber self, they are more likely to embellish when talking about themselves and some people even go to the extent of editing photos before they post them in order to remove any visible flaws. In the world of social media, everything is represented by a number, your follower count and your like count being the most prominent. People are going to like your posts more if you post more of what is considered “normal” and appealing. As the like count goes up, so can a person’s confidence. If it goes too far a person can literally fall in too deep and end up dedicating their entire life to increasing follower and like count. Say someone does put their all into it, and still continues to lose followers. This causes some issues with body image that can only be saved through time and a group effort. Social media is moving in the right direction by not censoring and shadow banning body positive content. With the growth that has been made over the past few years we are definitely on the right track to embracing all body types into societies definition of beautiful.

With all of the body positive content circulating, young women will be exposed to all body types instead of just what is deemed “perfect” by society. With tv shows and models becoming more inclusive, it allows for better role models for our youth. Hopefully this can reduce the number of young women suffering with eating disorders and depression. With a wider variety of content being shown on television even adults can start to see beauty for what it really is. Naya Rivera has a really beautiful quote that addresses this topic extremely well, “Butterflies can’t see their wings. They can’t see how beautiful they are, but everyone else can. People are like that”. We need to continue to lift each other up and radiate positive energy to the people around us. You never know what a person is going through behind the scenes, so do your best to treat everyone how you wish to be treated. Everyone has their own demons to overcome and when you’re constantly surrounded by mirrors that show you those demons, it’s hard to do something about it.
chunks.label: Body image, media influence, and body positivity
chunks.what_happened: The student discusses how television, social media, and societal beauty standards affect body image and eating disorders, referencing sociological concepts, research studies, celebrity examples, and the body positivity movement.

na4ebb5dc.title: Exploring Evolution and Religious Collective Consciousness

chunks.text:
Religion and the perception of culture is a crucial aspect of how collective consciousness came into being. In the Neurology of Religion, the author discusses the evolution that humans have experienced that have affected how they view religion. Religion is also an important aspect of collective consciousness through wanting to participate in what others are doing or wanting to be a part of something. Meanwhile, The Cultural Logic of Collective Representations discusses how multiple social groups or institutions were created through the participation in religious activities.

While these two authors notes correlate with each other on how religion and people relate to collective consciousness, it is important to keep in mind that there are two different social societies being discussed. An animalistic society such as the chimpanzees presented a type of collective consciousness that does not necessarily discuss religion but a gathering still. The other society being human and gathering to build a separate society among themselves was discussed in the other source. Both have the same idea and show how the earlier pre-evolved humans may have shown collective consciousness before building empires, governments, and advanced societies.
chunks.label: Collective consciousness and religion in readings
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on two readings discussing how religion, human evolution, and gatherings in animalistic versus human societies relate to collective consciousness.

n691bf622.title: Online Hostility and the Social Self

chunks.text:
In The Self, the I and the Me, Mead argues that the conception of self is highly dependent on the setting that you are in. A setting that has become more popular in today’s society is social media. Additionally, Erving Goffman believes online interactions are frequently toxic because people are not invested. In order to create a more positive online environment, society should focus more on the importance of this setting.

One of Mead’s main points is that the self is experienced out of internal dialogue called the “I” and the “me.” In experiences the “I” comes first and is the immediate reaction to a stimulus. The “me” is next and is the objective evaluation of the previous reaction. Going back to Goffman’s point about online interactions, it is possible that the reason for these hostile interactions is due to the lack of “me” in the situation. In online activities people are more likely to act faster and therefore not go through the “me.” This avoidance means that the persons initial reaction with any evaluation is what comes out into social media. This process is due to the fact that these interactions lack investment on both sides.

The conception of self is changes based on the setting you are in. In online or social media interactions there is larger likelihood for a negative exchange with others. This is due to the absence of the “me” within the internal dialogue. With more investment in these online exchanges, it is possible to create a more positive online network in society.
chunks.label: Mead and Goffman on self and online interactions
chunks.what_happened: The student discusses Mead's concept of the 'I' and the 'me' and Goffman's views on online interactions, explaining how the absence of the 'me' and lack of investment can lead to negative online exchanges.

When we think of power, the first thing we think of normally is not class level. In the document “Class in America,” Mantsios explains how people do not like to talk about class level when it has to do with privileges and oppression. In the United States we tend to avoid phrases that identify different levels of classes as it is seen as disrespectful. Even though people do not like using these terms, when it comes to dealing with strictly wealthy people, they use it as a symbol of power. The more money they have the more powerful they are among others in their class. In my experience at institutions such as public schools, class is also a touchy subject.

In public schools, class often comes up but not in direct ways. This is what makes it different from when class is brought up in “Class in America” and “Power in America”. In these two articles it applies to adults more than children in the instances they discuss. They identify these people as wealthy people that can give their children anything and everything that will later lead to their child having the same life and continuing that repeating process in some cases. These people begin to have influence over others as mentioned by Domhoff, the writer of “Power in America”. As mentioned before, in public schools, specifically high schools, children can see the differing classes among their peers but rarely put it into perspective. While a parent may see one child that is in a lower class as someone that is not going to succeed or get into a major university, another parent will see a child from a wealthier family and assume that that child is automatically going to get what they want in life. Meanwhile, children do not seem to hyper focus on this as much as adults do in these articles. I believe that the children begin to “show off” their class the older they get in some circumstances.

nb3e544fa.title: Challenging the American Dream and Mobility

chunks.text:
Is America truly the land of opportunity? With our class structure and how class correlates to success, I would argue that the phrase “land of opportunity” no longer fits America. The label “upper class” describes the small percentage of Americans who control the most wealth in the country. According to USA Today, the top 1% of the population controls 25-30% of the country's wealth. Due to this immense wealth, families in the upper class are subject to more opportunities and privileges, further increasing the wealth gap in the country.

The famous phrase, “the American dream” describes that with hard work and dedication, one can achieve immense success, no matter the social class they are birthed from. However, the truth often diverges from this belief. With the existence of the upper class, systematic inequalities have formed in America, making it extremely difficult for those in the lower classes to keep up.

One primary example of these inequalities is the schooling system. It is a proven fact that private schools are more effective for students than the average public school. However, due to the high cost of most private schools, more upper-class families can afford the tuition than lower-class families. The same goes for higher education institutions such as colleges. As college tuitions continue to rise, it has become much more difficult for middle to lower-class citizens to send their children to these universities.

Along with inequalities in the schooling system, the job market is also unequal for those in the middle and lower classes. If one is unable to pay for better education such as private schools or college, they are automatically behind those students whose family provides them with these opportunities. This leads to many upper-class citizens getting higher-paying jobs based on the family and class they are born into. Once obtaining a higher-paying job than someone with less education or opportunities, this cycle of social class repeats for the next generation.

There are millions of real-world examples of this cycle around the country. A child born into a rich political family will almost always be more successful than the son of a janitor. A student who goes to a private school, on average, will have higher test scores than a public school student. The student with higher test scores will almost always get into better colleges, and therefore be hired for better jobs than the student who began in the public school system. These are just broad generalizations and examples of the social class cycle in America working for wealthy families and against the less wealthy.

The people in these upper-class families are not to blame for these harsh realities, but they can push to make a difference. People of the upper class have much more authority than people of the middle or lower class. The upper class often consists of politicians, business owners, and entrepreneurs who can sway the public. These distinguished people can promote reform to the class system in America and help those less fortunate than themselves. One primary way I believe people of lower classes can be helped is by decreasing the costs of education across the country. All levels of education should be more affordable for each citizen no matter the class they are born into. Making education affordable will help create equal opportunities and give children of lower classes the opportunities needed to attend college and meet the requirements of many high-paying jobs. One more reform method that could help specifically those in the lower class is addressing the housing crisis in our country right now. Housing costs are at an all-time high, and rising each day. This makes it much harder for even middle-class families to afford a house along with essential goods and services needed to survive. Ways of improving the housing market could be to change the methods used to build houses or abolish rules for homeownership in certain areas across the country. These are just two examples of ideas the government and the upper class can push for to improve the lives of the citizens in the classes below them.

Overall, the social classes and large wage gap in America is a prominent and growing problem that needs to be addressed. Addressing these problems will take members of the upper class to speak out and promote change across the country. Those born into the lower class should not be predetermined for less success than a child born into the upper class. We must re-attain the ideals of the American dream and make our country the land of opportunity once more.
chunks.label: Analysis of social class and inequality in America
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on wealth disparity, educational inequalities, the job market, and potential reforms like reducing education costs and addressing the housing crisis.

n8ecd5940.title: Masculinity and Interpersonal High School Drama

chunks.text: The term “drama,” outside of the theatrical or literary sense, can often replace the “controversy,” but for situations that do not result in severe legal repercussions; “drama” is typically, but not limited to, a person-to-person ordeal that is glorified by a set group of people. Drama can range from two A-List celebrities arguing about the implications of a joke to an unnecessary fight between two close friends in a rural public school, but in both cases, a set group of people must be aware of this dilemma for it to be considered “drama” rather than personal bickering. People’s reactions to drama could be aggressive and mean towards the unfavorable party or completely unreactive, and a considerable influence on how people react to the drama is how their preferred side in the debacle appeals to the audience of the drama. The correlation between the reactions of both the participants and the audience is direct; the audience is likely to react as if moved by the same emotions portrayed by their preferred participant. Nevertheless, common patterns in people’s reactions to drama can be discovered when examining a selection of people based on set criteria; such criteria could be income, ethnicity, age, etc. However, one intriguing pattern for reactions to drama is found when examining people under the criteria of biological sex. More specifically, there seems to be a tendency that males are less likely to start drama with another male, and less likely to be an active audience member in male-to-male drama, compared to the exact opposite situation involving female-to-female drama. This is not to say that female groups are encouraged to be involved in drama, but that some sociological concepts suggest that male groups are prone to develop a collective consciousness that handles conflicting situations in a way that avoids drama from occurring.
chunks.label: Defining drama and gender differences
chunks.what_happened: The student defines the concept of drama and discusses general patterns in how males and females react to conflict.

chunks.text:
Now, the initial thought for this claim arose from my firsthand experiences in being involved in or discussing all types of drama, whether it is with friends, family, or the public. These observations are solely based on my personal interactions with males in high school to college, so, clearly, I cannot justify my argument around conclusions based on these observations. However, it is important to discuss why these claims came to be a rational conclusion for me because that could lead to discovering what underlying principles are affecting these scenarios.

So, reflecting on interactions of my own, I discovered that males tend to only start drama when there is a solid and justifiable reason, male drama climaxes marginally quicker than female drama, most males prefer to be a neutral spectator in all dramas, and males are more likely to resolve drama in a confrontational (sometimes violent) way than females. To start detailing my experiences, I will explain a common scenario that occurs with both sexes that could lead to drama: someone talks badly about another person. Surprisingly, a simple or rude critique often sparks conflict between people. However, even though both sexes are subject to rude words, my experience makes me believe that males usually do not create drama for minor personal attacks, while their female counterparts are more likely to start a drama from a similar level of personal attack. Most male dramas I experienced were instigated by issues that personally affected a male negatively (such as snitching to authority that results in disciplinary action) or issues that portray a male in a false light in a serious situation (attack on someone’s personality that could hurt them socially).

Nevertheless, if a male drama sparked from a minor personal attack, my experiences would argue that the drama would not stay relevant more for than a week usually; but if a female drama arose from a similar circumstance, the drama is likely to stay relevant for months. I would say that males dislike making a big deal about their drama in most cases, so they will attempt to calm the situation by being apathetic. But if a male chose not to be apathetic and instead was actively encouraging a drama to an audience for a minor personal attack, I would argue that most males would choose to just not be involved, unless they were close friends with someone involved in the drama. Still, if males get involved in a supportive role, the drama would usually be resolved quickly compared to female dramas. This is because male drama has the tendency to be resolved with direct confrontation, whether it is verbal or violent, and soon after the drama will become irrelevant. Regardless, this information does not explain why these trends are noticeable to an observer.
chunks.label: Reflecting on male versus female drama observations
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on general observations of male and female interactions in high school and college, generalizing about how drama starts, escalates, and resolves.

chunks.text:
In a study from 2006 by psychology professor Brett Stoudt titled “You’re Either In or You’re Out,” students at an all-male high school, Rockport, were studied and interviewed for the purpose of detailing the collective mindset and sociological trends of the students given the setting. The study found that Rockport experiences more student violence than co-ed public schools because of the strong encouragement of a hegemonic masculine mentality built within the school’s educational and social systems.

Hegemonic masculinity is a concept that describes a dominant form of masculinity that all males should strive to reach in terms of masculine norms. The concept is often reinforced by the functions of society, functions which are supported by censorship and peer discipline of others for not conforming to the norms; social functions that encouraged hegemonic masculinity were seen actively within the school. For the school, hegemonic masculinity was encouraged through the curriculum and academic competitiveness (functions), which led to strong criticisms from peers and sometimes exclusion from friend groups. This mentality can actively be noticed in the school’s sports program, where teammates often bully each other for faults, such as being a first-year student or not starting on the team. These conflicts would often be violent, lending a cause-and-effect explanation for why the school’s violence is more common. Even still, these conflicts would be handled in abrupt manners and the victims understood the reasoning for the conflict and accepted the violence because that is the norm; those who followed the norms would be considered “in” the hegemonic masculine mentality, and those not following norms were considered “out.” The study even suggests that hegemonic masculinity is good for the students since it builds a sense of self and sets a standard to follow if they seek a privileged status. Still, this concept is present outside of this specific example found within the study.
chunks.label: Stoudt's study on hegemonic masculinity
chunks.what_happened: The student explains a 2006 sociological study by Brett Stoudt regarding hegemonic masculinity and violence in an all-male high school.

chunks.text: Hegemonic masculinity can still be found in lots of portions of modern culture and can provide background for how males deal with drama. Like Rockport, my own high school had aspects of competitiveness and peer discipline that encouraged this concept. While not to the same level as Rockport, my high school (and likely all public high schools) builds hegemonic masculinity as a norm. However, I would argue that, even in the cases of Rockport, violence, bullying, and competitiveness found within a public school do not often result in drama. In fact, I would argue that hegemonic masculinity attempts censor drama through peer discipline and violence at any level. Causing drama would be seen as unnecessary and not ideal when a conflict is justified by this shared belief. This concept provides the sociological reasoning for why males tend to be involved in less drama than females.
chunks.label: Hegemonic masculinity suppressing drama
chunks.what_happened: The student explains how hegemonic masculinity functions in public high schools to suppress drama through peer discipline and violence.

chunks.text: In summary, male dramas occur less frequently than female dramas. This statement is proven through the sociological concept of hegemonic masculinity, which discourages male drama and reinforces the concept through violence. Although these ideas have focused on high school students, it does seem likely that hegemonic masculinity is prevalent in popular culture due to the number of institutions that support the concept and, comparatively, less popular male dramas occurring than female dramas. Furthermore, a debate about how males deal with drama versus females dealing with drama and mental health is often questioned. Do males deal with drama in a healthier and more just manner than females? Should hegemonic masculinity be encouraged if the benefits are significant?
chunks.label: Conclusion on gender drama and masculinity
chunks.what_happened: The student concludes the essay by summarizing findings about male and female drama and posing questions about hegemonic masculinity and mental health.

chunks.text:
The origins of the collective consciousness go very far back, not to the beginning of man, but to a random point in archeology when researchers found evidence of burial rituals and gifts. About 50,000 years ago is the time period where researchers found these rituals and gifts left with the dead and this time is the beginning of when researchers had proof of cultural and language developments all over the world. Once language and speech were established within the human race, this is when collective consciousness began to take hold of the populations. Once humans started speaking and writing it led to the asking of impossible questions like “what is the meaning of life?”

Language and speech brought up very important questions that could not really be answered, but other than those questions, humans began to experience culture and art development in their populations, which is still being found by archeologist today. The meaning of life puzzled the early humans, but the collective consciousness answered that question. Early homo sapiens did not know the meaning of life but they thought the community was the meaning and essence of life. This is the beginning of the collective consciousness that sociologist research.

This shared meaning that was found in the daily life of humans 50,000 years ago was seen through burial rituals and writing found by archeologist. This new collective consciousness led to basic human behavior of being one of a group. Language and speech paved the way for meaning being applied to everything in the world. Early humans were social animals that needed to be in groups and feel welcome. These groups had shared values that would later become known as the collective consciousness.
chunks.label: Origins and role of the collective consciousness
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on the historical origins of collective consciousness, explaining how language, burial rituals, and community helped early humans find meaning.

chunks.text:
The ‘looking glass self’ is the concept that we view ourselves based on how we believe that others are seeing us. We are continuously thinking about how we are perceived, and if we decide that someone has a bad perception of us then we choose to adopt those negative thoughts. But why do we care so deeply about how other people view us? It is part of our innate desire to be a part of something. The theory of the collective consciousness correlates to our perception of ourselves being directly tied to the opinions of the people around us.

These concepts compliment one another in the sense that the collective consciousness provides an explanation for the looking glass self. The looking glass self as a theory cannot be entirely explained without a reason as to why people care. Why people are so concerned over how they appear, why it is ingrained in humans to go along with the status quo. The collective consciousness answers these questions, people want to be liked and appear a certain way because everyone desires to be a part of something. People want to be accepted by society and have a sense of purpose within a larger group. Being a part of the collective consciousness provides the individual with security and meaning, this set of beliefs and traditions is essential to any society. These shared values bring people together and are the glue for a functioning society, people need things that can unite them.

One aspect of the looking glass self that the collective consciousness does not directly explain is how people take on how they believe they are being perceived. Cooley says that the individual will believe about themselves however they think someone else believes about them. That people value their peers’ opinions so much that if they have the inkling that someone does not like them, they will internalize those ideas and think about themselves negatively. This is a step further than simply valuing how you come across to the outside world. This means that the experience of the self is created only by interaction, meaning that we do not experience the self on our own. That who we are is formulated from how we want to be regarded and then how we believe to be regarded. The collective consciousness provides the spaces for the individual to experience the self. Without groups such as religion, schools, sports, etc. people would not have the opportunity to experience the self through interaction. Because we place such high importance on these groups, this is where people take into account how they are being received and judged.

To summarize my analysis, the collective consciousness and theory of the looking glass self go hand in hand when understanding each concept. The looking glass self shows the individual how they experience themselves and how other people play a key role in that. While the collective consciousness demonstrates why other people are such an integral part of understanding who we are and how we act.
chunks.label: Analyzing the looking glass self and collective consciousness
chunks.what_happened: The student explains how Cooley's concept of the looking glass self and the theory of collective consciousness complement each other in understanding how individuals view themselves and seek social acceptance.

chunks.text:
Throughout history man has been subjugating others, either for dominance in the group during early man’s history, or for dominance socially and economically. In recent years especially, race and equality have been heavily discussed in the news, making people discuss race and how racism has been used by America to discriminate and subjugate people of color. America was a country founded on slavery and oppression. When early colonist came over from Europe they almost immediately began subjugating and attempting to enslave the Native American people. This continued until the Native Americans were defeated and put on reservations, and for slaves that were brough over, life was difficult. Slaves were taken from their homes and forced to be the lowest in the social class in America. The weren’t treated like people, and even after they gained their freedom they were still oppressed by systematic racism in the United States. Still, after the civil rights movement and the change in the collective conscious about people of color, systematic racism and oppression still exist in America today. Throughout the years, especially back in high school, we would always see on the news of protests, police brutality, and acts of racism on the news. These events caused our community to change and become more polarized, leading to more acts of racism being caught in America. Throughout this I will be explaining how sociological concepts such as the concept of racial formations in the United States, white privilege in our social society, and discrimination against people of color in our society, will be used to show how a system of institutionalized racism has been constructed by the elite men at the top to subjugate people of color, and retain their hold on “their” society.

Now why does institutional racism exist? Why are people of color discriminated against, solely based of the color of their skin? Solely because they are the minority. In America at the moment, white people and people of European decent outnumber people of color. With white people being the majority, people of color have a much harder time at navigating through life due to the system put in place by white people. The system in place is designed for white people, and run by white people, allowing them to thrive. People of color also must deal with the fact that the system built is designed by older generations to discourage people of color. It’s created using the old, outdated ideas that were the norm back in the day, however now in America things have changed. We no longer have the extreme, brutal system that was in place in the past, however, institutional racism is still a large problem in America.

Race has always been a defining characteristic in American society. Your race used to be everything, and people have been designated into formations based on the color of their skin. America had laws implemented throughout its history to define a person’s race, and how that would affect their social standing. From 1982-1983, Susie Guillory Phipps unsuccessfully sued the state of Louisiana, to change her race from “black” on her birth certificate. Susie, a descendant of a white planter and a slave, was only 1/32 part African American, however was still designated as black the court. Now why put such an emphasis on the color of someone’s skin? We are all people the only difference between us is the amount of melanin we have in our skin. The reason being, to have race be a tool to social construct identity, where race is an important factor determined by social, economic, and political forces. By emphasizing the importance of your race in the United States, the majority group, being white people, have been able to stay on top of the social class by instituting laws that discriminate people of color, and help allow white Americans to excel. While many of the more extreme laws discriminating against people of color have been overturned, there are still cases of it in our society today. Just recently in our own state of North Carolina, republican party members were found to be rearranging political maps to group minorities together, allowing for them to win their districts. Activities like these have been used for centuries in America to disenfranchise people of color and restrict them from having an active role in politics.

Racial formations also affect the social norms of our society today. Just like when we saw the Joey Salads video in class, he played upon the stereotype formed by our society that black men are violent to get million of views on his YouTube channel. However, it later came to light that the entire video was an act used for entertainment. Stereotypes such as these have been used in America to keep control over the subjugated group. These stereotypes still influence the social standing of people of color in our society today. Many are grouped into categories just based of the color of their skin, to define them and group them into racial groups. Even old prejudices that are far out of date are still prevalent in our society. Studies done by students at the Princeton University highlighted prejudices that people of color have when competing for a job. In the study people of color were found to be more unlikely to get an interview, or even a call back, than white applicants. White applicants were so heavily favored that a white applicant with a record was given a call back, opposed to a black candidate without a record. Instances such as these are causes of the institutionalized racism in our country, as racial formations are one of the tools used to help promote systematic racism.

Now onto one of the most pressing concepts currently in our society: White privilege. As a white male, my life has been a lot easier than a person of color. I haven’t had to fight for the right to be myself and I haven’t had to fight for my rights just because my skin is a different color. Due to this it’s hard for me to witness white privilege. My experiences are normal to me because I grew up experiencing them. I grew up not fearing authority, not being afraid of being stereotyped based on the color of my skin, and I never had to go through what people of color go through in society. As mentioned before, the United States is a country meant for the white man to thrive. System is in place that allow white men to succeed and have a better chance of making it in life. White men are born with advantages that people of color just don’t have the opportunity to, and that’s exact what white privilege is. Many people don’t see their white privilege, however, almost everyone white person has it. Someone who’s white does not have to worry about if the police officer pulling them over will try to arrest them on bogus grounds, they also do not have to worry about being discriminated against during a job, at a school, or at any place in general. Now how does white privilege tie into the fact that there is a system of institutionalized racism put in place by the majority to oppress and discourage people of color? Well white privilege is an outcome of this system, it did not come before it. As the system was being created when settlers first came to America. As soon as Columbus first saw the new people in the new world, white privilege was born. Columbus and his men had greater technology and were able to subjugate the native people. Due to this action, white people privilege has evolved into how we now know it. It’s a tragic outcome of the system that’s in place. White people like me are treated above someone else, and to me that makes not logically sense. Why devalue someone based on the color of their skin, there’s no point in it. Someone different from myself can teach me an entire new culture and language. The world is fascinating a full of different things and people, why exclude and favor one over the other, it makes no sense.

While although I have never experienced racism in my life, it’s a huge issue in our society, and especially in recent years, the United States has become so polarized that racism and the inequality between white people and people of color is arguable the most important issue in our society. The three topics that I discussed are key topics that play a role in institutional racism in our society. Racial formations help to group people together and form racial identities. Through These racial identities, value is placed on them based of social, political, and economic forces, creating a society that values race when deciding trivial things like a job interview. White privilege plays a role in helping to keep the dominate race on top. It allows white people to stay ahead and on top, harming minorities chances of succeeding. Finally, the constant discrimination against people of color keeps them down and decreases their chances of success in our society. Every day, I see posts on Facebook and social media all the time about Black Lives Matter and other movements to end the inequality between us, racism is without a doubt the hottest button issue at the moment. By focusing on this issue and trying to end institutional racism, America can become equal and amazing society, however, to change America, we first need to change the collective conscious. We need to get ride of the outdated views that the United States was founded on and think differently. Thankfully I believe that America is already on this path. In my high school and especially now that I’m in college, I’ve realized that our generation has very little prejudices and very few students are racist. Most students go about their day not troubling themselves with matter involving race. We see people as people regardless of the color of their skin and choose to judge people off their personality and work ethic. In my mind, I see racism being almost nonexistent in the United States by the time in 60. By then my generation will be the “old people in charge” and hopefully our views and ways will be the norm.
chunks.label: Analysis of institutional racism and white privilege
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on the history and sociological concepts of institutional racism, racial formations, and white privilege in America, and considers how future generations might eliminate racial prejudice.

nb9cf0bd4.title: Challenging Gender Bias in STEM Fields

chunks.text: Science, engineering, technology, and math come together to create the acronym STEM which encompasses professions in all four areas. Historically, men have dominated these four areas of expertise while women have taken a back seat with fewer numbers enrolled in STEM courses and even fewer succeeding in the completion of said courses to continue onto a STEM profession. Even though the number of women in STEM fields has grown through the years these women still face barriers that make it harder to become leaders in their fields. If or when women make it into STEM professions, they face distortions in their representation in the media which makes it harder for their work to be seen without a feminine facade blocking its true value. Gender bias is only one aspect that these women face throughout all levels of their education. Women have been wrongfully represented in a field that they worked very hard to get into, though this is the case, women across the globe have begun to band together to change the face of STEM to be a more inclusive group of professionals. The media is an entity that holds much power in today’s society. Media outlets include newspapers, television networks, radio, social media, and many more. These media outlets can choose what and how to represent anything they want, for example, some news networks are more liberal and tend to cover negative events that involve conservative legislation. Several studies have been conducted to assess how the media portrays women in STEM, one, Mwenya Chimba and Jenny Kitzinger’s Bimbo or boffin? Women in science: an analysis of the representations and how female scientists negotiate cultural contradictions. During this study they looked at 12 prominent UK newspapers over a six-month period. They compiled a total of 7,903 articles about STEM with 51 of them being about specific scientists. When the researchers were assessing the representation within each article they looked at, “any reference to their relationship status, children, nationality, ethnic identity, and appearance.” They found that 16% of scientists that were mentioned were women with the other 84% being men. The findings suggested that women were more likely to have their age, relationship status, appearance, and parenthood mentioned somewhere in their description. This prompted an investigation into how women were presented in the description, specifically their physical characteristics, clothing, hairstyles, etc. The researchers found that many of the authors of these pieces focused on the scientists’ femininity with many physical descriptions. Some were described as “this petite, feisty communicator” and even “this 55-year-old academic’s mane of blonde hair” while the men that were written about had descriptions based on the “old scientists” such as Darwin or Einstein. This research shows that women were sexualized by the media despite their involvement in a very professional field. (Chimba, Kitzinger) The sexualization of women is just one way that women are misrepresented by the media in their STEM fields. The struggles that women endure does not start when they enter their fields, but instead it starts with their education, specifically starting at the high school level. Women are less likely to be enrolled in Advanced Placement courses compared to their male classmates. The factor that affects this is gender bias because women are generally not persuaded to enter STEM professions as much as men are. (Robnett) Rachael D. Robnett conducted a study entitled, Gender Bias in STEM fields: Variations in Prevalence and Links to STEM Self Concept. Robnett mentions the “STEM self-concept” many times in her work and she describes it as, “the extent to which individuals believe they are capable of excelling in STEM fields.” It is important to note this when reading Robnett’s findings that the STEM self-concept is greatly affected by gender bias. The results of this study found that 61% of women experienced gender bias “at least once in the past year.” (Robnett) The overwhelming majority described the type of bias they experienced as, “feeling as though you had to work harder than male students to be taken seriously” and even “hearing negative comments about girls’ and women’s STEM abilities.” (Robnett) Robnett then correlated the amount of gender bias experienced to the lessening of the STEM self-concept in women actively attaining education in STEM. After reviewing her results, Robnett addresses what can be done to lessen gender bias in STEM and even just trying to lessen the effects of the bias. One way that is described in her research is educating faculty and students of STEM classes on how to create a more inclusive environment to attract anyone to the field. Although the existence of gender bias varies based on the level of education and field in which they are studying, the existence in general is the problem that impacts women the most. (Robnett) Gender bias greatly impacts the STEM self-concept and self-esteem of these women that have courageously decided to enter these fields. The media representations of women in STEM accompanied by gender bias in the field makes for a difficult existence for women involved in the field. The struggles that women face are not new developments in society, these have been going on since the beginning of time. One early example of men thinking less of women was when Aristotle said, “We should regard women’s nature as suffering from natural defectiveness.” This shows that women have been inferior to men for hundreds of years. In Simone de Beauvoir’s work Women as Other he states that, “He is the Subject; he is the Absolute, She is the Other.” This idea of “women as other” is exactly what women in STEM are facing in today’s world. They are seen at the “other” in STEM fields because of the long history of them being male dominated. The connections between Aristotle and Beauvoir’s writings shows that women have been seen as inferior to men for much longer than society thinks. When they are sexualized by the media it is just a current way to classify them as the other. When gender bias is introduced, it is generally accepted by society because of the long history of pushing women out of leadership roles because they are the others of society. Though women have experienced struggles in STEM fields there has been a recent push for people to support the entrance of women into fields that a normally male dominated. Social media has made this a global movement to advance the presence of women in these male dominated professions. Reem Alkhammash conducted a study titled, It Is Time to Operate Like a Woman’: A Corpus Based Study of the Representation of Women in STEM Fields in Social Media. This study focuses on the emergence of “hashtag activism and digital feminism” that has taken the world by storm in recent years. Alkhammash describes the gender imbalance in STEM as a “leaky pipeline” and that means that women usually begin in STEM fields but then leak out and choose to not continue in the profession. She goes on to explain that women are disadvantaged by institutional and cultural factors in STEM, these factors are, the lack of female preparedness for STEM careers, poor female attitudes towards STEM since their childhood, and the absence of role models for women to follow and look up to. This is what sparked her research into digital activism to see how the world was turning the page on cultural norms and pushing for more female representation in these highly professional fields. Alkhammash’s research began with the acquisition of tweets from the social media platform, Twitter. She compiled tweets such as, “#womenintech, #GirlsWhoCode, #womenTechTalk, #womeninSTEM, #womenInSTEM, #womeninscience, #momscancode, and #ILookLikeASurgeon” (Alkhammash) In total, Alkhammash collected 14,611 tweets that ranged from October 31, 2017 to November 1, 2017 with most of the tweets coming from Portland, Oregon, US and Los Angeles, California, US. This immense number of tweets shows that the United States is leading in the digital activism that calls for more women to enter STEM as a profession. The digital activism is greatly helping women enter STEM fields and retain their careers for life. Another writing that supports the claim that women are entering STEM fields is Wendy M. William’s editorial, Underrepresentation of Women in Science: International and Cross Disciplinary Evidence and Debate. In her work she states that the number women that have transitioned to pursuing PhDs has been on the rise in recent years which means researchers and policy makers need to abandon the “leaky pipe” metaphor for the cause of women leaving STEM fields. She found that these new ideas included “campus childcare centers” instead of further enforcing gender quotas for hiring more women. Alkhammash and William’s writing shows that women have progressively been entering STEM, but they still have a long way to go. The fields of science, technology, engineering, and math or STEM as it is commonly known is a field that is predominantly male with a smaller number of females. This lack of women in these fields is caused by a multitude of factors including the lack of informative media coverage as opposed to coverage that focuses on their private life and gender bias that these women experience throughout their STEM education. Mwenya Chimba and Jenny Kitzinger explained that women are usually sexualized in their media coverage instead of being focused on because of their research or subject area. This unfair representation in the media is a contributing factor to the lack of women in the fields in question. Not only are they unfairly portrayed in the media, but they face bias based solely on their gender and never on their cognitive skill level. This gender bias that women face in STEM fields was researched by Rachael D. Robnett and she found that the increase in bias faced by women significantly decreases their chances of continuing in STEM education, which is unfair to them. Based on these struggles that women face getting into STEM, the world has responded by focusing a spotlight on recruiting and supporting women in STEM through social media and digital activism. This hashtag activism has inspired many women to pursue careers in STEM despite their struggles. Women in STEM is one the rise and is on its way to become a more equally represented profession. Sources Chimba, Mwenya and Kitzinger, Jenny. Bimbo or Boffin? Women in science: and analysis of media representations and how female scientists negotiate cultural contradictions. Sage Publications, 2010 Robnett, Rachael. Gender Bias in STEM Fields: Variation in Prevalence and Links to STEM Self-concept. Sage Publications. 2015 Williams, Wendy. Editorial: Underrepresentation of Women in Science: International and Cross-Disciplinary Evidence and Debate. Frontiers in Psychology. 2018 Alkhammash, Reem. It is Time to Operate Like Women’: A Corpus Representation of Woman in STEM Fields in Social Media. 2019
chunks.label: Gender bias and media representation in STEM
chunks.what_happened: The student presents an academic essay reviewing research, philosophy, and digital activism related to women's underrepresentation and portrayal in STEM fields.

n272e0dcc.title: Growing Up Blind to Class Inequality

chunks.text:
The class system in the United States is basically split up into three groups, the lower class, middle class, and the upper class. The lower class is characterized by those who are in poverty or below the official poverty line in the US. The middle class is commonly referred to as those who live comfortably and have opportunities that allow them to advance. The final and most influential class is the upper class, which can be split further into sections like the power elite. These classes have been around as long as the US itself but the inequality that was seen is only growing between the three different classes. The class systems are growing further apart from each other with each passing year but not much has been done to try and stop it.

The readings describe a very divided class system that the US has produced over a couple hundred years, the lower class is left with no opportunities to try and advance in class while the middle class lives comfortably in its professional class system, and finally the upper-class controls about one third of the whole countries wealth. In Gregory Montsois 2006 work, Class in America, he debunks several myths that the American public has accepted as truth, for example, he debunks that in the US every citizen has equal opportunity to succeed. Montsois goes on to explain that the evidence shows that the class inequality is growing which can be seen when analyzing income levels from the three classes.
chunks.label: US class system and course readings
chunks.what_happened: The student outlines the three main classes in the US and summarizes readings by Gregory Mantsios about growing class inequality and debunked myths about equal opportunity.

chunks.text: While I was growing up in an all-white household, we never really discussed those in poverty and those who are the “power elite” (as Domhoff describes them), but my siblings and I did understand that our family was middle class and living comfortably with a few hardships that would affect us. The collective conscious that was created in my household was one that did not focus on racial inequalities or class inequalities but that led me to not fully understand those issues until I was much older. The class system that was established by my collective conscious was one that thought people always lived comfortably and didn’t have anything to overly worry about which is not was Domhoff describes in his work, Power in America, he brings to light something that I never knew about growing up, the “power elite.” The power elite that Domhoff describes is people who have direct influence in our government via different methods such as lobbying. This class system that was in these readings was very different from what my collective conscious knew already.
chunks.label: Growing up in a middle-class household
chunks.what_happened: The student grew up in an all-white middle-class household where racial and class inequalities were not discussed, leaving the student unaware of the 'power elite' and broader class struggles until reading sociological texts later.

chunks.text: The system in the us that establishes the lower, middle, and upper classes is one that is very intricate and usually misunderstood because of the collective conscious. The mainstream media removed class issues from their broadcasts leading people to not think they were an issue, but now we can see that it is a growing issue that has resurfaced and needs fixing. The inequality between the US economic classes is something that is ongoing and is in urgent need of addressing.
chunks.label: Media influence and class inequality
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on how the class system is misunderstood due to the collective consciousness and mainstream media, concluding that growing economic inequality urgently needs fixing.

chunks.text:
We live in a fast paced society focused around convenience and what will reap the most benefits for us. Most Americans eat fast food one to three times a week. In a world where healthy, organic food is readily available in most places, why do we choose to eat unhealthy and unsatisfying meals? This is due to McDonaldization, which is this formula that has been created to turn the highest profit for the business and rope in the most consumers. However, this concept is not entirely unfamiliar to our society. Rationalization laid the groundwork for McDonaldization to take form, McDonaldization took Rationalization from only the workplace to nearly every aspect of our lives.

McDonaldization is based on four main attributes; efficiency, calculability, predictability and control. McDonald’s has drastically reduced the time that it takes for a customer to order and eat a meal. Mechanisms like drive-thru windows and order ahead apps cut down on time and employee exertion. They have also been successful due to the predictability of the meal, a Big Mac is the same in New York as it is in California. Corporate giants such as Walmart and Amazon have followed suit in the “McDonald’s way of doing things”. The business has a large amount of control as well. In fast food restaurants you are expected to know what you want to eat when you get to the window as well as have your money ready to pay. This pressure and control is put on the consumer so that they may have the most efficient work flow.

Rationalization laid the groundwork for McDonaldization. Both theories are focused on the benefits of the corporation. Rationalization seeks to give the employer the highest profit and eliminate choice for the consumer. Both theories eliminate creativity and the human process of work as an expression. Instead work’s only purpose is to create what is most profitable rather than what the worker desires. In essence, these ideas reflect a quantity over quality mindset. Pre-Industrial Revolution the goods that were produced were handmade, took longer to create, and were influenced by the creator’s desire. The main difference between the two ideas is that Rationalization revolves only around the workplace. McDonaldization has worked its way into all aspects of our life, especially the social space.

As mentioned before, there are multiple large corporations that have adopted the McDonaldization business model. We are so surrounded by convenience that as a group we perhaps don’t even realize the structures put in place for efficiency. Amazon is a great example of this, you can order anything you want at the click of a button. They have even gone so far as to remember your card information and shipping address so that all you have to press is buy, without a second thought. As well as with their various devices such as Alexa, all you have to do is tell Alexa to order you the desired item. The practices and results of these theories have vastly increased as our society has progressed, it is natural to expect them to continue to rise and nearly eradicate the concept of “small businesses”. It has been proven that when given the choice, most people opt for the bigger corporation that provides them with the easiest access to the desired product rather than seeking out a small business who takes longer but creates a higher quality product or experience.

McDonaldization has revolutionized the way we experience our day to day lives and this would not have been possible without the movement of Rationalization during the Industrial Revolution. It can be debated if McDonaldization has more positive or negative outcomes in terms of the way individuals shop, eat, and interact with each other. It could be argued that McDonaldization has reaped far more benefits for the large institutions rather than the market. These theories have certainly ushered in the era of convenience and created a large reliance on technology to make our lives easier. The implementation of Rationalization and McDonaldization are undeniably prevalent in our everyday routines and have forever altered what the public expects from big businesses.
chunks.label: McDonaldization and Rationalization in modern society
chunks.what_happened: The student reflects on the sociological theories of McDonaldization and Rationalization, explaining how large corporations prioritize efficiency, calculability, predictability, and control at the expense of quality and small businesses.

n296dd65c.title: Analyzing White Privilege and Collective Consciousness

chunks.text: White privilege fits some characteristics of collective consciousness. This can be proved through Durkheim idea of collective consciousness and McIntosh’s perspective and experiences of white privilege. However, there is some characteristics of collective consciousness that do not fit white privilege. One of these characteristics is that is not into brought into existence through ritual. But due to the other characteristics and examples it should be confirmed that white privilege is a collective consciousness.
chunks.label: White privilege as collective consciousness
chunks.what_happened: The student analyzes whether white privilege fits the characteristics of collective consciousness using concepts from Durkheim and McIntosh.

chunks.text:
Emile Durkheim defined the term “The Collective Conscious” as the conditions of a subject within a society, and how said individual views themselves in society. This collective consciousness creates a shared group of ideas, beliefs, and collective knowledge in a society. The collective conscious defines almost all things in a society, whether correct or incorrect. For example, the ancient Egyptians once believed that each day, the sun god Ra would pull the Sun on his chariot each day, and would circle into the underworld at night, and come back in the morning pulling the sun. Back then, this was the truth of their society. They fully believed that a God would pull the sun because that’s what the collective conscious believed. Now we know that the Sun simply circles the Earth and doesn’t disappear into the underworld each night. However, this shows the power the collective conscious has over a society. It dictates the daily lives and beliefs of the society. The collective conscious also dictates what is good and bad in a society. An example of this was back in ancient times, same sex couples were much more excepted, such as in ancient Greece. Then for a period of time when Christianity was the reigning religion, it was deemed a sin and was extremely frowned upon. However now in recent times, same sex couples have been more accepted and embraced. The collective consciousness imprints on everyone in a society, dictating what morals people have and ultimately dictating what is right and wrong in society. While the collective conscious dictates a society, it also binds the society together. By believing in the same things, the group of people is brought closer together, and safety is found in a group that believes the same thing. This is how societies are formed. By a group of people coming together, having the same beliefs and ideas, solidarity is formed and a society forms. Now with this many things can affect the collective conscious and can influence and change it. For example, religion has a large affect on a collective conscious. Religious leaders have the power to influence the collective consciousness greatly. Especially during medieval time, the pope or other priests could simply change what they want and call it God’s will. By doing so they changed the ideas that many believed in and were able to change the collective conscious. Back to how the acceptance of same sex couples has changed over time, this is also a good example of how the collective conscious changes overtime with the views of the people. Overall, the collective conscious can change at a whim with everyday events and change with the views of the people. Specifically in recent years the collective conscious changes almost every year. With events that happen and just everyday fads and beliefs, the collective conscious changes. An important part of the collective conscious is also that the collective conscious must exist in a society, or a society cannot form. Without everyone agreeing and believing the same, then conflict would erupt in our society. We are starting to see this in our society as the population grows. More and more beliefs and values are starting to appear within our society, causing some conflict between groups to see which side will overpower the other and become the dominant collective consciousness. While in our society, it’s important to have an individual identity and to not follow copy the collective conscious, by varying from the conscious, it sparks conflict between groups. Therefore, in major societies such as ours, these “pocket collective consciousness” form. By a subgroup of people forming with the same beliefs and ideals, a new collective consciousness forms going against the major collective consciousness. In this essay I will be tying in the beliefs on the collect consciousness that Durkheim presents with the ideas that Harari had when writing 21 Lessons for the 21st Century, showing how the ideas are similar and how each tie into our modern society.

As I have already covered Durkheim’s theories regarding the collective consciousness, I will now be discussing Harari’s ideas regarding religion. In his book, Harari discusses how religion ties into modern society, and how in the past, religion was used to solve technical problems, policy problems, and identity problems. He discusses how in ancient times religion was used to decide when to plant crops using a divine calendar, how religion has dominated policy decisions in the past and in today’s world, such as how in Islamic countries around the world such as Iran, the Quran dictates many aspects of their laws, and how identity problems were controlled by religion, such as what to believe and what morals a person should have. However, many of these ideas and the overall control of religion have begun to dimmish from our society.

Religion has begun to separate from technical problems through the advancement of science. Instead of using a divine calendar to predict when the best time to plant crops were, we now know when the best seasons to plant are and the perfect conditions to plant crops are. In ancient times we simply did not have the technology and scientific knowledge to predict weather conditions, tell the quality of the soil to a deeper level, or be able to tell if the farmland was still fertile. However now with these technologies we are now able to do all of these things, making religion being involved in technical matters obsolete. Religion was also used to dictate medicine in ancient times. People often believed that when they were sick, it was a sign from God and that going to church and praying hard enough, that it would eventually go away. Now with our current technology, we know of microbes and how to properly deal with disease and illness. In technical matters like these, science and technology made religion obsolete.

Karl Marx was especially against religion, because he viewed that it had no real grounds to exist in a society. He believed that religion simply got in the way of life and manipulated people into believing ideas and changing their values, just to appease the religion itself. While communism and his ideas aren’t really prevalent in our society today, his view that religion shouldn’t be as connected within a government is starting to come to fruition. In country in Europe for example, religion is almost entirely taken out of law and is pretty much separated from the church. In the United States, for a long time up until recent history, religion was supposed to be separate from the state, but still played a major role in laws. While the church did not have direct power to make laws and govern the nation, the people who made the laws were religion, causing their views to rub off on the laws created. However, in our modern society, more and more laws are being passed going against religion, showing how it is becoming less involved in policy making. Eventually, religions ideas may leave law entirely and policy will be made without a second thought to religion.

With identity problems, the case is slightly different. As humans, we all have morals and values regardless of religion in our lives. We are taught to be kind to others and help others in need, however this is also taught in many religions as well. However, religion forms ones identity in a sense. Religion has been used throughout the years to develop customs and a cultural identity in a group. With different religions forming around the world, each with its separate customs and believes, people tend to be more hostile towards others of a different religion. A good example of this is Islamic people and Jewish people. Throughout history the group have been in conflict over their views, especially in recent years with the creation of Israel. Both sides argue the land belongs to their ancestral people, and that they should be entitled to it, sparking conflict between the two. These conflicting identities stemming from their own religion have caused numerous wars. Harari explains further how religion is not the savior of religion, but actually its downfall. By having all of these conflicting identities among so many people, true equality and peace cannot be achieved.
